**ἔνθʼ** (adverb): "there," locative, marking the place where the sign appeared. **ἐφάνη** (verb): 3rd singular aorist passive indicative of φαίνω, "appeared" or "was seen." **σῆμα** (noun): nominative singular neuter, "sign" or "portent," the divine omen. **δράκων** (noun): nominative singular masculine, "serpent" or "dragon," subject of the omen. **δαφοινός** (adjective): nominative singular masculine, "blood-red" or "crimson," modifying the serpent's back.

There appeared a great portent: a serpent with blood-red back.
309: **σμερδαλέος** (nom. sg. masc. adj.) "terrible, dreadful" - modifies δράκων from the previous line. **αὐτὸς** (nom. sg. masc. intensive pron.) "himself" - emphasizes Ὀλύμπιος as the agent. **Ὀλύμπιος** (nom. sg. masc. adj./subst.) "the Olympian" - Zeus as sender of the portent. **ἧκε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of ἵημι) "sent forth, made appear." **φόως** (acc. sg. neut.) "light, into the light" - poetic form for φάος, indicating motion into daylight.
310:
**βωμοῦ** (gen. sg. masc. of βωμός): "of the altar," genitive of separation. **ὑπαΐξας** (aor. act. ptc. nom. sg. masc. of ὑπαΐσσω): "darting from beneath," indicating swift movement away from the altar. **πλατάνιστον** (acc. sg. masc. of πλατάνιστος): "plane tree," goal of motion. **ὄρουσεν** (aor. act. ind. 3rd sg. of ὄρνυμι): "he rushed, sprang toward," main verb expressing the serpent's attack.

The serpent darts out from beneath the altar and rushes toward the plane tree (where the sparrow's nestlings are located).
311:
**ἔνθα** (adverb): "there," locating the scene in the plane tree. **στρουθοῖο** (noun, genitive singular, from στρουθός): "of a sparrow," specifying the bird species. **νεοσσοί** (noun, nominative plural): "nestlings, young birds." **νήπια** (adjective, nominative plural neuter): "helpless, innocent," modifying **τέκνα** (noun, nominative/accusative plural neuter): "children, offspring." 

The line describes helpless sparrow nestlings in the tree, emphasizing their vulnerability before the serpent's attack.
312: **ὄζῳ** (dat. sg. masc. of ὄζος): "on a branch" – dative of location. **ἀκροτάτῳ** (dat. sg. masc. of ἀκρότατος, superlative of ἄκρος): "topmost, highest." **πετάλοις** (dat. pl. neut. of πέταλον): "under/among the leaves" – dative of place. **ὑποπεπτηῶτες** (nom. pl. masc. perfect participle of ὑποπτήσσω): "cowering, crouching down." The young sparrows are cowering under the leaves on the topmost branch.
313:
**ὀκτώ, ἀτὰρ μήτηρ ἐνάτη ἦν ἣ τέκε τέκνα·**

**ὀκτώ** (numeral, indeclinable): "eight" – referring to the number of children devoured. **ἀτάρ** (particle): "but, and" – marks transition to the mother. **ἐνάτη** (adjective, nominative feminine singular): "ninth" – the mother as the ninth victim. **τέκε** (verb, 3rd singular aorist active indicative of τίκτω): "bore, gave birth to." The line contrasts the eight children with their mother, who was the ninth victim after bearing them.
314:
**ἔνθα** (adverb): "there, then" – temporal/locative adverb marking the scene. **ὅ γε** (demonstrative pronoun, nominative singular masculine): "he" – refers to Apollo. **ἐλεεινά** (adjective, accusative plural neuter): "pitiable, wretched" – modifies the participle, describing the victims' state. **κατήσθιε** (verb, 3rd singular imperfect active indicative, κατεσθίω): "was devouring, consuming" – depicts Apollo methodically killing them. **τετριγῶτας** (perfect active participle, accusative plural masculine, τρίζω): "shrieking, crying out" – describes Niobe's children screaming as they die.

Apollo devours/destroys the pitiable, shrieking children in a scene of divine vengeance for
315: **μήτηρ** (nom. sg. fem., "mother") is the subject; **ἀμφεποτᾶτο** (3rd sg. impf. mid., ἀμφιπέτομαι, "was flying around") describes her circling flight; **ὀδυρομένη** (nom. sg. fem. pres. mid. part., ὀδύρομαι, "lamenting") modifies μήτηρ; **φίλα τέκνα** (acc. pl. neut., "dear children") is the object of her grief. The mother bird flies around lamenting her beloved offspring.
316:
**τὴν δʼ ἐλελιξάμενος πτέρυγος λάβεν ἀμφιαχυῖαν.**

- **ἐλελιξάμενος** (aor. mid. ptc. nom. sg. masc., < ἑλίσσω): "having coiled around," describes the serpent's action
- **λάβεν** (aor. act. indic. 3rd sg., < λαμβάνω): "seized," main verb
- **πτέρυγος** (gen. sg. fem., < πτέρυξ): "by the wing," genitive of means or part seized
- **ἀμφιαχυῖαν** (pres. act. ptc. acc. sg. fem., < ἀμφιαχέω): "
317:
**αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ κατὰ τέκνα φάγε στρουθοῖο καὶ αὐτήν**

Key words: **ἐπεί** (conjunction) "when, after"; **τέκνα** (neut. acc. pl. of τέκνον) "children, young"; **φάγε** (3rd sg. aor. ind. act. of ἔδω/ἐσθίω) "ate, devoured"; **στρουθοῖο** (gen. sg. of στρουθός) "of the sparrow"; **αὐτήν** (fem. acc. sg. of αὐτός) "her (the mother bird) herself." "But when [the serpent] devoured the young of the sparrow and her herself."
318:
**τὸν μὲν ἀρίζηλον θῆκεν θεὸς ὅς περ ἔφηνε·**

**τὸν** (demonstrative pronoun, acc. sing. masc.): "him/it," referring to the serpent from the previous line. **ἀρίζηλον** (adjective, acc. sing. masc.): "very visible, conspicuous," modifying τὸν. **θῆκεν** (verb, 3rd sing. aor. act. indic. of τίθημι): "made, turned (into)." **ἔφηνε** (verb, 3rd sing. aor. act. indic. of φαίνω): "revealed, made appear." The god who revealed the serpent-omen also made it conspicuously visible by turning it to stone.
319:
**λᾶαν** (acc. sg. masc., λᾶας): "stone," object of ἔθηκε. **ἔθηκε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic., τίθημι): "made (him into)," main verb. **Κρόνου πάϊς** (gen. + nom., Κρόνος, παῖς): "son of Kronos," i.e., Zeus. **ἀγκυλομήτεω** (gen. sg. masc., ἀγκυλομήτης): "of crooked counsel," epithet modifying Κρόνου (genitive).

The son of crooked-counseled Kronos turned him into stone; Zeus petrified the victim as divine punishment or transformation.
320:
**ἡμεῖς** (pronoun, nom. pl.): "we" — subject of the verb, contrasted with the monstrous creatures.

**ἑσταότες** (perfect active participle, nom. pl. masc., from ἵστημι): "standing" — describes the speakers' posture as witnesses.

**θαυμάζομεν** (verb, 1st pl. imperfect active indicative, from θαυμάζω): "we were marveling/wondering at" — expresses astonishment.

**οἷον** (relative adverb/exclamatory): "what sort of thing" or "how great a thing" — introduces the object of wonder.

**ἐτύχθη** (verb, 3rd sg. aorist passive indicative, from τεύχω): "had been made/fashioned" — refers to the extraordinary event or object that
321:
**ὡς** (adv.): "thus, as" - introduces the comparison or manner clause. **πέλωρα** (nom. pl. neut.): "portents, monstrous signs" - subject of εἰσῆλθε, from πέλωρ referring to the serpents. **θεῶν** (gen. pl.): "of the gods" - attributive or possessive genitive with πέλωρα. **εἰσῆλθε** (3rd sg. aor. indic.): "entered, came into" - from εἰσέρχομαι, with shortened ε for meter. **ἑκατόμβας** (acc. pl. fem.): "hecatombs, sacrifices" - direct object, the offerings the portents entered.

The line describes how the divine portents (serpents) entered the sacrificial hecatombs,
322: **Κάλχας** (nom. sg. m., proper name) "Calchas" - the Greek seer; **αὐτίκα** (adv.) "immediately, straightway"; **ἔπειτα** (adv.) "then, thereupon"; **θεοπροπέων** (pres. part. nom. sg. m., θεοπροπέω) "prophesying, interpreting the divine will"; **ἀγόρευε** (3rd sg. impf. act., ἀγορεύω) "spoke, declared." Calchas immediately began to speak as a prophet, declaring the gods' will.
323: **τίπτε** (τίπτε, interrog. adv.): "why?"; **ἄνεῳ** (ἄνεως, adj., nom. pl. masc.): "speechless, silent"; **ἐγένεσθε** (γίγνομαι, aor. indic. 2nd pl.): "did you become"; **κάρη κομόωντες** (periphrastic pres. part., nom. pl. masc. from κομάω): "long-haired" (lit. "wearing hair on the head"). Hector rebukes the silent Trojans: "Why have you become speechless, long-haired Achaeans [sic: Trojans]?"
324: **ἡμῖν** (pronoun, dative plural, "to/for us") **τόδε** (demonstrative pronoun, neuter accusative singular, "this") **τέρας** (noun, neuter accusative singular, "portent, omen") **μέγα** (adjective, neuter accusative singular, "great") **μητίετα** (epithet, vocative singular, "counselor, wise") **Ζεύς** (noun, nominative singular, "Zeus"). Zeus the counselor has revealed this great portent to us; the datives frame the audience while the demonstrative points to the sign just witnessed.
325:
**ὄψιμον ὀψιτέλεστον, ὅου κλέος οὔ ποτʼ ὀλεῖται.**

**ὄψιμον** (acc. sg. neut., "late-coming") and **ὀψιτέλεστον** (acc. sg. neut., "late-fulfilled") are compound adjectives modifying an understood noun like "portent"; **ὅου** (gen. sg. rel. pron., "of which") introduces a relative clause; **κλέος** (nom. sg. neut., "glory/fame") serves as subject; **ὀλεῖται** (fut. mid. 3rd sg. of ὄλλυμι, "will perish"). The line emphasizes that though the omen's fulfillment will come late, its fame will be imperishable.
326:
**Key words:** 
- **κατὰ** (prep. + acc.): "down, completely" governing τέκνα, intensifying the verb
- **τέκνα** (n. acc. pl.): "children, young" direct object of φάγε
- **φάγε** (v. 2nd aor. act. ind. 3rd sg. ἐσθίω): "he/it devoured, ate"
- **στρουθοῖο** (n. gen. sg.): "of the sparrow" possessive genitive with τέκνα and αὐτήν
- **αὐτήν** (pron. acc. sg. fem.): "her, herself" (the mother bird), second object of φάγε

The serpent devoured completely the sparrow's children and the mother herself, with κατά emphasizing the totality of consumption, f
327:
**ὀκτώ, ἀτὰρ μήτηρ ἐνάτη ἦν ἣ τέκε τέκνα,**

**ὀκτώ** (indeclinable numeral): "eight" – the number of sparrow chicks devoured. **ἀτάρ** (conjunction): "but, and" – marks contrast or transition. **μήτηρ** (nominative singular, fem.): "mother" – the parent sparrow. **ἐνάτη** (nominative singular, fem. ordinal): "ninth" – she was the ninth victim. **τέκε** (3rd sg. aorist indicative, τίκτω): "bore, gave birth to" – relative clause explaining her role as mother of the **τέκνα** (accusative plural, neuter): "children."
328:
**ὣς** (adverb): "thus, so" - introducing the comparison or conclusion.

**τοσσαῦτα** (demonstrative adjective, neuter accusative plural): "so many" - modifying ἔτεα, correlating with the nine years just mentioned.

**ἔτεα** (noun, neuter accusative plural): "years" - direct object indicating duration.

**πτολεμίξομεν** (verb, 1st plural future indicative): "we shall wage war" - from πτολεμίζω, indicating future military action.

The line means: "Thus we shall wage war here for so many years," connecting the prophecy of nine years' duration to the siege of Troy.
329: **τῷ δεκάτῳ** (δέκατος, -η, -ον): dative singular masculine/neuter adjective, "in the tenth (year)," agreeing with an understood ἔτει. **πόλιν** (πόλις, -εως, ἡ): accusative singular feminine noun, "the city," direct object of αἱρήσομεν. **αἱρήσομεν** (αἱρέω): first person plural future active indicative, "we will take/capture." **εὐρυάγυιαν** (εὐρυάγυια, -ης, ἡ): accusative singular feminine adjective, "broad-streeted/with wide streets," modifying πόλιν.
330: **κεῖνος** (ekeinos): demonstrative pronoun, nominative singular masculine, "that one" (referring to Calchas). **τὼς** (tōs): adverb, equivalent to οὕτως, "thus, in this way." **ἀγόρευε**: 3rd singular imperfect active indicative of ἀγορεύω, "he spoke, he declared." **τελεῖται**: 3rd singular present passive indicative of τελέω, "is being fulfilled, is coming to pass." The line recalls Calchas's earlier prophecy, emphasizing that his predictions are now coming true.
331:
**Key words:** *μίμνετε* (μίμνω, 2nd pl. pres. imperat. act.) "remain, stay"; *πάντες* (πᾶς, nom. pl. masc.) "all"; *ἐϋκνήμιδες* (ἐϋκνήμις, nom. pl. masc.) "well-greaved," epithet of warriors; *Ἀχαιοί* (nom. pl. masc.) "Achaeans, Greeks."

Agamemnon exhorts all the well-greaved Achaeans to remain at Troy, urging collective perseverance in the siege.
332:
**αὐτοῦ** (adv.): "right here, in this place" — indicating remaining in position at Troy.

**εἰς ὅ κεν** (prep. + rel. pron. + modal particle): "until" — temporal phrase introducing a future condition (with ἄν/κεν + subjunctive).

**ἄστυ** (n. nom./acc. sg.): "city" — the object of ἕλωμεν, referring to Troy.

**Πριάμοιο** (n. gen. sg.): "of Priam" — possessive genitive modifying ἄστυ.

**ἕλωμεν** (v. 1st pl. aor. subj. act.): "we might take, capture" — from αἱρέω, expressing purpose/anticipated result with κεν.

The line urges
333:
**ὣς** (adverb): "thus, so" – marks the close of Nestor's speech.
**ἔφατο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of φημί): "he spoke" – the subject is the wise counselor from the previous line.
**Ἀργεῖοι** (nom. pl. masc.): "the Argives" – the Greek forces responding.
**ἴαχον** (3rd pl. aor. act. indic. of ἰάχω): "shouted, cried out" – their vocal approval.
**νῆες** (nom. pl. fem. of ναῦς): "ships" – the hollow ships resound in response to the Achaean roar, as the next line confirms.
334: **σμερδαλέον** (adverb, "terribly, dreadfully") modifies **κονάβησαν** (3rd pl. aorist indicative of κοναβέω, "resounded, rang out"), describing the ships' reverberating noise. **ἀϋσάντων** (aorist active participle gen. pl. of ἀΰω, "shouting") with **Ἀχαιῶν** (gen. pl., "of the Achaeans") forms a genitive absolute: "as the Achaeans shouted." The ships resounded terribly under/from the shouting Achaeans.
335: **μῦθον** (accusative singular of μῦθος): "speech" or "plan," object of ἐπαινήσαντες. **ἐπαινήσαντες** (aorist active participle, nominative plural masculine of ἐπαινέω): "having praised" or "approving," modifying an understood subject (the Achaeans). **Ὀδυσσῆος** (genitive singular of Ὀδυσσεύς): "of Odysseus," possessive genitive with μῦθον. **θείοιο** (genitive singular of θεῖος): "godlike" or "divine," epithet modifying Ὀδυσσῆος. The Achaeans approved the speech of godlike Odysseus.
336: **τοῖσι** (dat. pl. demonstrative pronoun) "to them"; **μετέειπε** (3rd sg. aor. indic. of μετα-ειπεῖν) "spoke among/after"; **Γερήνιος** (nom. sg. adj.) "Gerenian" (epithet); **ἱππότα** (nom. sg. m. noun/epithet) "horseman, knight"; **Νέστωρ** (nom. sg. proper noun) "Nestor." Nestor of Gerenia, the horseman, then spoke among them in response.
337: **ὦ πόποι** (interjection): exclamation of dismay or reproach, "alas" or "oh my." **ἦ** (particle): "truly" or "indeed," emphasizing the statement. **παισὶν** (noun, dative plural of παῖς): "children" or "boys," dative of comparison with ἐοικότες. **ἐοικότες** (perfect active participle, nominative plural of ἔοικα): "being like" or "resembling." **ἀγοράασθε** (verb, 2nd person plural present middle indicative of ἀγοράομαι): "you gather" or "you hold assembly." The line reproaches the assembled men for conducting their debate like children.
338:
**νηπιάχοις** (dat. pl. masc., νηπίαχος): "childish ones, infants" – dative of comparison or reference, emphasizing immaturity.

**οἷς** (dat. pl. relative pronoun): "to whom" – introduces relative clause.

**μέλει** (3rd sg. pres., μέλω): "it is a care, it matters" – impersonal verb governing genitive (πολεμήϊα ἔργα).

**πολεμήϊα ἔργα** (nom./acc. pl. neut., πολεμήϊος + ἔργον): "warlike deeds, martial works" – subject of μέλει in the sense "for whom warlike deeds are no concern."

The line condemns the Greeks as childish, to whom war matters not at all.
339: **πῇ** (interrogative adverb) "where? whither?"; **συνθεσίαι** (nominative plural, feminine noun from σύνθεσις) "compacts, covenants"; **ὅρκια** (nominative plural, neuter noun from ὅρκιον) "oaths, sworn pledges"; **βήσεται** (3rd singular future middle, from βαίνω) "will go, will come to pass"; **ἥμιν** (dative 1st person plural pronoun) "for us, to us." The speaker questions where their covenants and sworn oaths will end up, implying their dissolution or nullification.
340: **ἐν πυρὶ** (prep. + dat.): "in fire" — idiomatic for destruction or futility. **βουλαί** (nom. pl., βουλή): "counsels, plans." **γενοίατο** (3rd pl. aor. opt. mid., γίγνομαι): "may they come to be, may they end up" — optative expressing a wish or potential consequence. **μήδεά** (nom. pl., μῆδος): "plans, designs." The line laments that all plans and counsels of men may come to nothing (literally "end up in fire") if oaths are broken.
341:
**σπονδαί** (nom. pl. fem. of σπονδή): "libations, treaty-oaths"; **ἄκρητοι** (nom. pl. fem. of ἄκρητος, -ον): "unmixed (with water), pure"; **δεξιαί** (nom. pl. fem. of δεξιά): "right hands, pledges"; **ἐπέπιθμεν** (1st pl. plpf. mid. of πείθω): "we trusted in, relied upon." 

The line lists what would be destroyed in fire: the libations of unmixed wine and the clasping of right hands in which the Greeks had placed their trust when making their treaty with the Trojans.
342:
**αὔτως** (adverb): "in vain, fruitlessly, to no purpose" — modifies the manner of their quarreling.

**ἐπέεσσ(ι)** (noun, dative plural of ἔπος): "with words, in words" — dative of means, indicating the instrument of their dispute.

**ἐριδαίνομεν** (verb, 1st plural present indicative of ἐριδαίνω): "we quarrel, we wrangle" — the main verb describing their ongoing contentious debate.

**μῆχος** (noun, nominative/accusative singular neuter of μῆχος): "means, remedy, device" — the object they fail to find, with **οὐδέ τι** ("not any") negating it.

The line conveys their futile quarreling in words without finding any solution or means forward
343: **εὑρέμεναι** (aorist infinitive, active, from εὑρίσκω) "to find"; **δυνάμεσθα** (1st plural present middle/passive indicative from δύναμαι) "we are able"; **πολὺν χρόνον** (accusative of duration of time) "for a long time"; **ἐνθάδʼ** (adverb) "here"; **ἐόντες** (nominative plural masculine present participle from εἰμί) "being." The line expresses their inability to find any solution despite being here for a long time.
344: **Ἀτρεΐδη** (vocative singular, "son of Atreus") addresses Agamemnon directly. **σὺ δʼ** (nominative singular pronoun + particle, "and you") emphasizes the subject. **ἔχων** (present active participle, nominative masculine singular, "holding/keeping") governs **ἀστεμφέα βουλήν** (accusative singular, "unwavering counsel/purpose"). **ὡς πρίν** ("as before") indicates continuity of steadfast leadership.
345:
**ἄρχευʼ** (ἄρχευε, 2nd sg. pres. impv. act. of ἀρχεύω): "be leader, command" (with dative)
**Ἀργείοισι** (dat. pl. masc. of Ἀργεῖος): "to/for the Argives"
**κατὰ** (prep. + acc.): "throughout, in"
**κρατερὰς** (acc. pl. fem. of κρατερός): "mighty, violent"
**ὑσμίνας** (acc. pl. fem. of ὑσμίνη): "battles, combats"

The verse commands Agamemnon to continue leading the Argives through mighty battles.
346: **τούσδε** (pronoun, acc. pl. masc. of ὅδε): "these (men)," i.e., the quarreling Greek leaders. **φθινύθειν** (verb, pres. inf. of φθινύθω): "waste away, perish." **ἕνα καὶ δύο** (numerals, acc.): "one and two," i.e., "both" or "the pair." **τοί** (particle): "who (indeed)," relative/demonstrative introducing a characterizing clause. Zeus tells Athena to let these two (Agamemnon and Achilles) waste away, who among the Achaeans [are causing strife].
347: **νόσφιν** (adverb): "apart, separately" — governs the participle, indicating isolated action. **βουλεύωσι** (3rd pl. pres. subj. act. of βουλεύω): "they deliberate, make plans" — jussive subjunctive in indirect discourse. **ἄνυσις** (nom. sg. fem. noun): "accomplishment, fulfillment" — subject of ἔσσεται. **ἔσσεται** (3rd sg. fut. mid. of εἰμί): "will be" — predicting the outcome. The line warns that whatever few Achaeans plot apart will achieve no fulfillment.
348: **πρὶν** (adverb): "before" (governing the following infinitives). **Ἄργος** (noun, accusative singular neuter): "Argos" (object of *ἰέναι*). **ἰέναι** (verb, present infinitive): "to go." **Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο** (noun phrase, genitive singular masculine): "of aegis-bearing Zeus" (epithet modifying Zeus). The line states they should not return to Argos before determining whether Zeus's promise is false or true.
349: **γνώμεναι** (aorist infinitive, from γιγνώσκω) "to know, ascertain"; **ψεῦδος** (nominative neuter singular noun) "falsehood, lie"; **ὑπόσχεσις** (nominative feminine singular noun) "promise, undertaking"; **εἴ τε ... εἴ τε** (correlative conjunctions) "whether ... or"; **οὐκί** (negative particle) "not." The line presents an indirect question to determine whether the promise is false or not.
350:
**φημί** (1st sg. pres. act. indic.) "I declare/assert"; **κατανεῦσαι** (aor. act. infin. of κατανεύω) "to nod assent"; **ὑπερμενέα** (acc. sg. masc. of ὑπερμενής) "exceedingly mighty"; **Κρονίωνα** (acc. sg. of Κρονίων) "son of Kronos" (Zeus). 

Thetis asserts that Zeus nodded in assent to her petition, employing the verb **φημί** with infinitive construction to emphasize the certainty of the divine promise.
351: **ἤματι** (dat. sg. neut. of ἦμαρ) "on the day"; **τῷ** (dat. sg. neut. of ὁ, demonstrative/relative) "that" or "on which"; **ὅτε** (temporal conjunction) "when"; **νηυσὶν** (dat. pl. of ναῦς) "the ships"; **ὠκυπόροισιν** (dat. pl. fem./masc. of ὠκύπορος) "swift-faring"; **ἔβαινον** (3rd pl. impf. of βαίνω) "they embarked/went." The line refers to the day when the Achaeans boarded their swift ships, setting the temporal context for Zeus's prophesied nod.
352:
**Ἀργεῖοι Τρώεσσι φόνον καὶ κῆρα φέροντες**

**Ἀργεῖοι** (nom. pl. masc., "Argives"): the Greeks. **Τρώεσσι** (dat. pl. masc., "for/to the Trojans"): dative of disadvantage. **φόνον** (acc. sg. masc., "slaughter") and **κῆρα** (acc. sg. fem., "death/doom"): objects of φέροντες. **φέροντες** (nom. pl. masc. pres. part., "bringing/bearing"): the Argives bring slaughter and death to the Trojans.
353: **ἀστράπτων** (pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. masc., ἀστράπτω) "flashing lightning"; **ἐπιδέξιʼ** (adv., ἐπιδέξια) "on the right" (with elision); **ἐναίσιμα** (adj. acc. pl. neut., ἐναίσιμος) "favorable, propitious"; **σήματα** (noun acc. pl. neut., σῆμα) "signs, portents"; **φαίνων** (pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. masc., φαίνω) "showing, displaying." Zeus sends lightning on the right, displaying favorable omens to encourage the Argives against the Trojans.
354:
**τὼ** (adverb): "therefore," "for that reason" – inferential particle drawing conclusion from Zeus's favorable sign.

**πρίν** (adverb/conjunction): "before," "until" – temporal marker indicating the condition that must be met first.

**ἐπειγέσθω** (verb): 3rd person singular present middle/passive imperative of ἐπείγω, "let him hasten" – jussive imperative forbidding premature departure.

**οἶκον δὲ νέεσθαι** (noun + particle + infinitive): "to return homeward" – οἶκον (accusative of direction) with νέεσθαι (present middle infinitive of νέομαι), completing the prohibition against going home before fulfilling the condition stated in the next line.
355: **πρίν** (adv.) "before"; **τινα** (indef. pron., acc. sg. masc.) "some (man)," object of κατακοιμηθῆναι; **Τρώων** (noun, gen. pl.) "of the Trojans," partitive genitive; **ἀλόχῳ** (noun, dat. sg. fem.) "with the wife," dative of accompaniment; **κατακοιμηθῆναι** (aor. inf. pass.) "to sleep with," complementing the prohibition. The line forbids Greeks from hastening home before sleeping with some Trojan's wife, part of Agamemnon's exhortation for vengeance.
356: **τίσασθαι** (aorist middle infinitive of τίνω) "to exact vengeance for" governs **Ἑλένης** (genitive of Ἑλένη) "Helen's" (objective genitive). **ὁρμήματά** (neuter accusative plural of ὅρμημα) "impulses, provocations" and **στοναχάς** (accusative plural of στοναχή) "groanings, lamentations" are coordinated objects connected by **τε...τε** "both...and." The infinitive continues the purpose clause: the Greeks must avenge both Helen's abduction and the sufferings it caused before anyone returns home.
357: **εἰ δέ τις** (if anyone): conditional particle with indefinite pronoun nominative singular. **ἐκπάγλως** (exceedingly, excessively): adverb intensifying the desire. **ἐθέλει** (wishes): 3rd singular present active indicative of ἐθέλω. **οἶκον δὲ νέεσθαι** (to return homeward): accusative of goal with present middle infinitive of νέομαι (return). The line introduces a conditional warning about anyone who desires too eagerly to go home.
358:
**ἁπτέσθω** (3rd sg. pres. mid. impv. of ἅπτω): "let him lay hold of, touch" — a command construction. **ἧς** (fem. gen. sg. of ὅς): possessive pronoun "his own." **νηὸς** (gen. sg. of ναῦς): "ship," governed by ἁπτέσθω. **ἐϋσσέλμοιο** (gen. sg. of ἐΰσσελμος): compound epithet "well-benched." **μελαίνης** (fem. gen. sg. of μέλας): "black," standard Homeric ship epithet. 

Agamemnon warns that whoever excessively desires to return home should grasp his own well-benched black ship, so that he may meet death and doom before the others
359:
**Key words:** ὄφρα (conjunction) "so that, in order that"; πρόσθʼ (adverb, elided πρόσθεν) "before, ahead of"; θάνατον (acc. sg. masculine noun) "death"; πότμον (acc. sg. masculine noun) "fate, doom"; ἐπίσπῃ (2nd sg. aorist subjunctive middle, ἐφέπω) "you may draw upon yourself, incur."

The line expresses a purpose clause: "so that you may draw death and doom upon yourself before the others," warning of the peril of seizing the ship first.
360:
**ἀλλά** (ἀλλά, conjunction): "but" — strong adversative introducing a contrasting exhortation.

**αὐτός** (αὐτός, intensive pronoun, nominative singular masculine): "yourself" — emphasizing the subject's personal responsibility.

**μήδεο** (μήδομαι, present middle imperative, 2nd singular): "devise, plan well" — the verb governs strategic thought, here with adverb **εὖ** ("well").

**πείθεο** (πείθομαι, present middle imperative, 2nd singular): "obey, be persuaded by" — governing the dative **ἄλλῳ** ("another").

The speaker urges the addressee both to plan wisely himself and to heed others' counsel.
361:
**Key words:** ἀπόβλητον (adjective, nominative neuter singular) "thrown away, fruitless, in vain"; ἔπος (noun, nominative neuter singular) "word, speech"; ἔσσεται (future middle indicative, 3rd singular of εἰμί) "will be"; ὅττί κεν εἴπω (relative clause with modal particle) "whatever I may say."

The line means "the word will not be fruitless/in vain, whatever I may say"—a solemn assurance that the speaker's advice will prove valuable.
362: **κρῖνον** (κρίνω): 2nd sg. aorist imperative active, "marshal, separate, organize." **φῦλα** (φῦλον): acc. pl. neuter, "tribes" (administrative divisions). **φρήτρας** (φρήτρη/φρήτρα): acc. pl. feminine, "phratries, clans" (kinship groups within tribes). Agamemnon is urged to organize his troops by tribal and clan divisions so that units of kinsmen will fight together and support one another.
363:
**Key words:** φρήτρη (nom. sg. fem.) "phratry/clan"; ἀρήγῃ (3rd sg. pres. subj. act. of ἀρήγω) "may aid, help"; φῦλα (nom. pl. neut.) "tribes"; φύλοις (dat. pl. neut.) "to/for tribes."

Nestor advises organizing troops by kinship groups so that "phratry may aid phratry, and tribes [aid] tribes," with the datives φρήτρηφιν and φύλοις expressing mutual support among these social divisions.
364:
**εἰ δέ κεν ὣς ἕρξῃς καί τοι πείθωνται Ἀχαιοί**

**εἰ** (conjunction): if, introducing a future-more-vivid condition. **κεν** (particle): modal particle (= ἄν) with subjunctive in protasis. **ἕρξῃς** (2nd sg. aor. subj. act. of ῥέζω/ἔρδω): "you should do/act," referring to Agamemnon organizing troops by tribes and clans. **πείθωνται** (3rd pl. pres. subj. mid. of πείθω): "they obey," the Achaeans submitting to his command. **Ἀχαιοί** (nom. pl. masc.): "the Achaeans
365:
**γνώσῃ** (verb, 2nd sg. future middle indicative of γιγνώσκω): "you will know/recognize." **ἡγεμόνων** (noun, genitive plural of ἡγεμών): "of the leaders/commanders." **κακός** (adjective, nominative singular masculine): "cowardly/base/bad." **λαῶν** (noun, genitive plural of λαός): "of the people/troops."

"Then you will recognize which of the leaders is cowardly and which of the troops," establishing the purpose of the proposed test to distinguish brave from cowardly fighters at all ranks.
366:
**Key words:** ἠδέ (conj.) "and, or"; ἐσθλός (adj. nom. sg. masc.) "good, brave"; ἔῃσι (pres. subj. 3rd sg. of εἰμί) "may be"; κατὰ σφέας (prep. + acc. pronoun) "according to themselves, each for himself"; μαχέονται (pres. mid./pass. 3rd pl. of μάχομαι) "they fight."

Agamemnon continues that he will recognize who among the leaders and men is brave, since they will fight "according to themselves" (i.e., individually or each man showing his true mettle in battle).
367: **γνώσεαι** (γιγνώσκω): 2nd sg. future middle indicative, "you will know/learn." **θεσπεσίῃ** (θεσπέσιος): dat. sg. fem., "by divine ordinance/god-sent fate." **πόλιν** (πόλις): acc. sg., "city," object of ἀλαπάξεις. **ἀλαπάξεις** (ἀλαπάζω): 2nd sg. future active indicative, "you will sack/destroy." Agamemnon tells the seer he will learn whether it is by divine will that the Greeks cannot sack the city, or by human failings in war.
368: **ἦ** (particle): "or" introducing an alternative question. **ἀνδρῶν** (noun, gen. pl. of ἀνήρ): "of men," genitive of source/cause. **κακότητι** (noun, dat. sg. of κακότης): "because of cowardice/badness," dative of cause. **ἀφραδίῃ** (noun, dat. sg. of ἀφραδίη): "because of folly/thoughtlessness," paired with κακότητι. **πολέμοιο** (noun, gen. sg. of πόλεμος): "of war," objective genitive with ἀφραδίῃ. The line asks whether failure to sack Troy results from the troops' cowardice and tactical foolishness in battle rather than divine protection.
369:
**ἀπαμειβόμενος** (present middle participle, nominative singular masculine, from ἀπαμείβομαι): "answering in turn, replying"
**προσέφη** (3rd singular aorist indicative active, from προσφημί): "addressed, spoke to"
**κρείων** (present active participle, nominative singular masculine, from κρείω, used as epithet): "ruling, lordly"
**Ἀγαμέμνων** (nominative singular proper noun): "Agamemnon"

Agamemnon, lord of men, answers Nestor's speech with a formal reply, the participle ἀπαμειβόμενος marking the exchange pattern typical of Homeric dialogue.
370: **ἦ** (particle): asseverative, "truly, indeed"; **μάν** (particle): strengthening/affirmative, "certainly"; **ἀγορῇ** (noun, dative singular from ἀγορή): "in assembly/speech-making"; **νικᾷς** (verb, 2nd singular present indicative from νικάω): "you conquer, surpass"; **γέρον** (noun, vocative singular from γέρων): "old man." The speaker concedes that the old man surpasses the sons of the Achaeans in assembly/oratory, with emphatic particles (ἦ μάν, αὖτε) reinforcing the acknowledgment.
371: **αἲ γάρ** (particle + particle): "would that, if only" — expressive wish construction. **Ζεῦ** (nom. masc. sg., voc.): vocative of Zeus, "O Zeus." **πάτερ** (nom. masc. sg., voc.): "father," in apposition to Zeus. **Ἀθηναίη** (nom. fem. sg., voc.): vocative of Athena. **Ἄπολλον** (nom. masc. sg., voc.): vocative of Apollo. The speaker calls upon the three principal gods in a wish formula, introducing a prayer for assistance.
372:
**τοιοῦτοι** (toioûtoi): demonstrative adjective, nominative plural masculine, "such (men), of such a kind"

**δέκα** (déka): indeclinable numeral, "ten"

**συμφράδμονες** (sumphádmones): noun, nominative plural masculine, "counselors, advisers" (from συμ- "together" + φράδμων "one who plans")

**εἶεν** (eîen): optative, 3rd plural of εἰμί, "might be, would be" (expressing a wish)

Agamemnon wishes that ten such counselors among the Achaeans might be his, continuing his praise of Nestor's strategic wisdom.
373: **τώ** (adverb, "then," "therefore") introduces the apodosis. **κε** (modal particle) with **ἠμύσειε** (3rd sing. aorist optative middle of ἀμύω, "would be sacked/taken") forms a potential optative construction. **πόλις** (nominative singular, "city") is the subject. **Πριάμοιο ἄνακτος** (genitive singular, "of lord Priam") modifies πόλις. The line expresses a hypothetical consequence: "then would the city of lord Priam be taken."
374: **χερσίν** (dative plural of χείρ): "by the hands" – dative of agent with passive participles. **ὑφ'** (preposition + dative): "under, by" – reinforces instrumental sense. **ἡμετέρῃσιν** (dative plural feminine of ἡμέτερος): "our" – possessive adjective modifying χερσίν. **ἁλοῦσα** (aorist passive participle, feminine nominative singular of ἁλίσκομαι): "having been captured/taken." **περθομένη** (present passive participle, feminine nominative singular of πέρθω): "being sacked/destroyed" – both participles modify πόλις from the previous line, describing Troy's capture and destruction at Achaean hands.
375:
**ἀλλά** (ἀλλά, conjunction): "but" – strong adversative marking a contrast with the previous thought.

**αἰγίοχος** (αἰγίοχος, -ον, nominative singular masculine adjective): "aegis-bearing" – standard Homeric epithet for Zeus.

**Κρονίδης** (Κρονίδης, -ου, nominative singular masculine): "son of Kronos" – patronymic identifying Zeus.

**ἄλγεʼ** (ἄλγος, -εος, accusative plural neuter): "griefs, pains" – object of ἔδωκεν.

**ἔδωκεν** (δίδωμι, 3rd singular aorist active indicative): "gave, has given" – main verb expressing Zeus's bestowal of suffering.
376:
**Key words:** 
- **ὅς** (relative pronoun, nom. sg. masc.): "who" — refers back to Zeus
- **μετά** (preposition + acc.): "into" — direction into which something is cast
- **ἀπρήκτους** (adjective, acc. pl. fem.): "fruitless, profitless" — modifies ἔριδας
- **ἔριδας** (noun, acc. pl. fem.): "quarrels, disputes"
- **βάλλει** (verb, 3rd sg. pres. act. indic.): "casts, throws"

Zeus repeatedly casts the speaker into pointless quarrels and strife, emphasizing divine responsibility for human conflict.
377:
**καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼν Ἀχιλεύς τε μαχεσσάμεθʼ εἵνεκα κούρης**

*ἐγών* (1st sg. nom. pronoun) "I"; *Ἀχιλεύς* (nom. sg.) "Achilles"; *μαχεσσάμεθα* (1st pl. aor. mid. indic. < μάχομαι) "we fought, quarreled"; *εἵνεκα* (prep. + gen.) "on account of, because of"; *κούρης* (gen. sg. < κούρη) "girl, maiden." The speaker recalls how he and Achilles quarreled over a girl (Briseis), establishing a precedent for the current dispute.
378:
**ἀντιβίοις** (adj. dat. pl. masc./neut.): "hostile, opposing" - modifies ἐπέεσσιν. **ἐπέεσσιν** (noun dat. pl.): "with words, speeches" - dative of means. **ἦρχον** (verb 1st sg. imperf.): "I began, I was the first" - from ἄρχω. **χαλεπαίνων** (participle nom. sg. masc. pres.): "being angry, raging" - from χαλεπαίνω, modifying ἐγώ. 

The line means: "with hostile words, and I was the first to be angry."
379: **εἰ** (conjunction): "if" — introducing a future condition. **μίαν** (fem. acc. sg. of εἷς, μία, ἕν): "one," modifying βουλήν (understood). **βουλεύσομεν** (1st pl. fut. indic. of βουλεύω): "we shall deliberate/plan together." **οὐκέτι** (adverb): "no longer," negating future action. **ἔπειτα** (adverb): "thereafter/afterwards." The line expresses a conditional hope: "But if ever we shall plan together as one, then no longer afterwards..." (implying Trojan plans will be thwarted).
380: **Τρωσὶν** (dat. pl. of Τρῶες): "for the Trojans" — dative of disadvantage. **ἀνάβλησις** (nom. sg. fem.): "postponement, delay" — subject of the sentence. **κακοῦ** (gen. sg. neut. of κακός): "of evil" — objective genitive with ἀνάβλησις. **ἔσσεται** (3rd sg. fut. mid. of εἰμί): "will be." **ἠβαιόν** (adv.): "even a little bit, at all" — with the negative "not even slightly." The line means once the Greeks unite in counsel, there will be no postponement of disaster for the Trojans, not even a little.
381: **νῦν** (adverb): "now." **ἔρχεσθʼ(ε)** (2nd pl. pres. impv. mid., ἔρχομαι): "go, come!" **δεῖπνον** (acc. sg. neut. noun): "dinner, meal." **ξυνάγωμεν** (1st pl. aor. subj. act., ξυνάγω): "let us join, bring together" (purpose clause with ἵνα). **Ἄρηα** (acc. sg. masc., Ἄρης): "Ares," here metonymy for "battle, war." Agamemnon urges the Greeks to take their meal so they may join battle, with Ares representing the coming combat.
382:
**Key words:** *θηξάσθω* (aorist middle imperative, 3rd sg. of θήγω) "let him sharpen"; *δόρυ* (nom./acc. neut. sg.) "spear"; *ἀσπίδα* (acc. fem. sg.) "shield"; *θέσθω* (aorist middle imperative, 3rd sg. of τίθημι) "let him set/prepare."

The anaphoric *εὖ* ("well") emphasizes thorough preparation: each warrior should sharpen his spear well and ready his shield well before the coming battle.
383:
**Key words:** εὖ (adverb) "well"; ἵπποισιν (dative plural of ἵππος) "to the horses"; δεῖπνον (accusative singular neuter noun) "meal, dinner"; δότω (3rd singular aorist imperative active of δίδωμι) "let him give"; ὠκυπόδεσσιν (dative plural adjective modifying ἵπποισιν) "swift-footed."

The line continues Agamemnon's exhortations for battle preparation, commanding that each warrior properly feed his swift horses before engaging in combat.
384:
**Key words:** εὖ (adverb) "well, carefully"; ἅρματος (noun, genitive singular, neuter) "of chariot," from ἅρμα; ἀμφίς (adverb) "on both sides, around"; ἰδών (participle, aorist active nominative singular masculine) "having looked to," from ὁράω; μεδέσθω (verb, imperative present middle 3rd singular) "let him attend to, take thought for," from μέδομαι. 

Each man should look carefully around his chariot and attend to the business of war.
385:
**ὥς** (adverb): "thus, in this way" – marks purpose/result of the previous exhortation.

**πανημέριοι** (adjective, nominative plural masculine): "all day long, for the whole day" – from πᾶν + ἡμέρα, describing the duration of battle.

**στυγερῷ** (adjective, dative singular masculine/neuter): "hateful, dreadful" – modifies Ἄρηϊ, emphasizing the grim nature of warfare.

**κρινώμεθʼ** (verb, 1st plural present middle subjunctive): "we may be separated/decided" – from κρίνω, here meaning "engage in battle," with Ἄρηϊ as dative of means.

**Ἄρηϊ** (noun, dative singular): "by
386:
**Key words:** παυσωλή (noun, nom. sg. fem.) "respite, pause"; μετέσσεται (verb, 3rd sg. fut. mid.) "will come between, intervene"; οὐδʼ ἠβαιόν (adv.) "not even a little, not at all." 

The line asserts that there will be no respite or pause, not even briefly, in the coming battle—emphasizing the relentless nature of the combat until nightfall intervenes.
387:
**Key words:** νύξ (nom. sg. fem.) "night"; ἐλθοῦσα (aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. fem. from ἔρχομαι) "coming, having come"; διακρινέει (fut. act. 3rd sg. from διακρίνω) "will separate, will decide"; μένος (acc. sg. neut.) "fury, fighting spirit." 

The line means "unless night coming separates the fury of men"—a conditional clause indicating that only nightfall will halt the relentless battle.
388:
**ἱδρώσει** (fut. act. indic. 3rd sg. of ἱδρόω, "to sweat") "will become sweaty"; **τευ** (enclitic indef. pronoun gen. sg., "of someone") "of someone"; **τελαμών** (nom. sg., "shoulder-strap, baldric") "the shield-strap"; **ἀμφί** (prep. + dat., "around") "around"; **στήθεσφιν** (dat. pl. of στῆθος, "chest, breast") "the chest." 

The shield-strap of someone will become sweaty around his chest (from the exertion of battle).
389:
**ἀσπίδος ἀμφιβρότης, περὶ δʼ ἔγχεϊ χεῖρα καμεῖται·**

*ἀσπίδος* (gen. sg. of ἀσπίς): "of the shield," dependent on ἀμφιβρότης. *ἀμφιβρότης* (nom. sg. adj.): "covering both sides," or "worn around," epithet describing the shield-strap. *ἔγχεϊ* (dat. sg. of ἔγχος): "with the spear," instrumental dative. *χεῖρα* (acc. sg. of χείρ): "hand," subject accusative. *καμεῖται* (3rd sg. fut. mid. of κάμνω): "will grow
390: **ἱδρώσει** (future, 3rd sing. of ἱδρόω): "will sweat" — the horse laboring in battle. **τευ** (enclitic genitive, σύ): "of someone/anyone" — indefinite possessive. **ἐΰξοον** (adjective, acc. sing. neut.): "well-polished" — modifying ἅρμα. **ἅρμα** (noun, acc. sing. neut.): "chariot" — object being pulled. **τιταίνων** (present participle, nom. sing. masc. of τιταίνω): "straining/pulling" — the horse's exertion. The verse describes a warrior's horse sweating as it strains to pull the polished chariot.
391:
**ὃν δέ κʼ ἐγὼν ἀπάνευθε μάχης ἐθέλοντα νοήσω**

**ὃν** (relative pronoun, acc. sing. masc.) "whom"; **κε** (particle) modal "κέ" (= ἄν); **ἀπάνευθε** (adverb/preposition + gen.) "far from, away from"; **ἐθέλοντα** (present participle, acc. sing. masc. from ἐθέλω) "willing, wishing"; **νοήσω** (1st sing. aor. subjunctive from νοέω) "I perceive, notice." "But whomever I perceive wishing (to remain) away from battle..."
392: **μιμνάζειν** (pres. inf., μίμνω): "to remain, linger"; **παρὰ νηυσὶ κορωνίσιν** (prep. + dat. pl.): "beside the curved ships" (*κορωνίς* = curved, beaked); **οὔ οἱ** (neg. adv. + dat. sg. pronoun): "not for him"; **ἔπειτα** (adv.): "thereafter, then." Agamemnon threatens that whoever he finds lingering by the ships will find no escape from dogs and vultures (anticipating the next line).
393:
**ἄρκιον** (neuter nominative singular, adjective): "sufficient," "enough" – serving as predicate with ἐσσεῖται. **ἐσσεῖται** (3rd singular future of εἰμί): "will be" – future indicative forming impersonal construction. **φυγέειν** (aorist active infinitive of φεύγω): "to escape," "to flee" – complementing ἄρκιον in an infinitive construction. **κύνας** (masculine accusative plural): "dogs" – direct object of φυγέειν. **οἰωνούς** (masculine accusative plural): "birds," "vultures" – second object coordinated with κύνας.

The line states "it will be sufficient to escape the dogs and birds (of prey)," expressing the hope of avoiding becoming carrion.
394:
**ὣς ἔφατʼ, Ἀργεῖοι δὲ μέγʼ ἴαχον ὡς ὅτε κῦμα**

Key words: **ἔφατʼ** (3rd sg. aor. ind. mid. of φημί, "he spoke"); **Ἀργεῖοι** (nom. pl. masc., "the Argives"); **ἴαχον** (3rd pl. aor. ind. of ἰάχω, "they shouted"); **ὡς ὅτε** (comparative formula, "as when"); **κῦμα** (nom. sg. neut., "wave"). The simile compares the Argives' shouting response to a wave, introducing an extended maritime comparison.
395: **ἀκτῇ** (dat. sg. fem. of ἀκτή): "on/against the headland/shore"; **ἐφʼ** (prep. ἐπί with elision): "upon"; **ὑψηλῇ** (dat. sg. fem. of ὑψηλός): "high, lofty"; **κινήσῃ** (3rd sg. aor. subj. act. of κινέω): "should stir up, set in motion"; **Νότος** (nom. sg. masc.): "the South Wind." The simile continues: the Achaeans' shouting is compared to waves against a high headland whenever the South Wind comes and stirs them up.
396: **προβλῆτι** (dat. sg. masc. pres. part. of προβάλλω): "jutting out," modifying σκοπέλῳ. **σκοπέλῳ** (dat. sg. masc. noun): "cliff, rock." **κύματα** (nom. pl. neut. noun): "waves," subject of λείπει. **λείπει** (3rd sg. pres. indic. of λείπω): "leaves, abandons." The line describes a projecting cliff that the waves never leave—an image of perpetual assault, completing the simile of Paris facing the Greeks' relentless attacks.
397:
**παντοίων** (gen. pl. adj. of παντοῖος) "of all kinds," modifies ἀνέμων. **ἀνέμων** (gen. pl. of ἄνεμος) "of winds," genitive of source or agent. **ὅτʼ ἂν** (ὅτε + ἄν) "whenever," introduces an indefinite temporal clause. **γένωνται** (3rd pl. aor. subj. mid. of γίγνομαι) "they come to be/arise," subjunctive with ἄν expressing general condition. 

The line describes winds of every kind, whenever they arise from one direction or another, completing the simile of the rock constantly battered by waves and winds.
398: **ἀνστάντες** (ἀνίστημι, aorist participle nominative plural masculine): "having stood up, arising." **ὀρέοντο** (ὄρνυμι, imperfect middle 3rd plural): "they stirred themselves, set out." **κεδασθέντες** (κεδάννυμι, aorist passive participle nominative plural masculine): "having been scattered, dispersing." **κατὰ νῆας**: "throughout the ships" (distributive). The Achaeans rise and make their way back, dispersing among their ships after the assembly.
399:
**κάπνισσάν** (aorist, 3rd plural, καπνίζω): "they made burnt offerings," ritual smoking/sacrifice to the gods. **κατὰ κλισίας**: "throughout the huts," prepositional phrase indicating distribution across the camp shelters. **δεῖπνον** (accusative singular neuter): "dinner/meal," object of ἕλοντο. **ἕλοντο** (aorist middle, 3rd plural, αἱρέω): "they took (for themselves)," i.e., they partook of their meal.

The Achaeans, dispersed to their ships, performed sacrifice in their individual quarters and then took their evening meal.
400:
**ἄλλος δʼ ἄλλῳ ἔρεζε θεῶν αἰειγενετάων**

**ἄλλος** (nom. sg. m., "one") and **ἄλλῳ** (dat. sg. m., "to another"): correlative pronouns indicating reciprocal distribution among the Greek warriors. **ἔρεζε** (3rd sg. impf. mid., < εὔχομαι, "prayed"): each man made prayer. **θεῶν** (gen. pl., < θεός, "of the gods") and **αἰειγενετάων** (gen. pl. m., < αἰειγενέτης, "ever-living, eternal"): descriptive genitive with the compound epithet emphasizing divine immortality. Each warrior prayed to a different immortal god
401: **εὐχόμενος** (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg. masc. of εὔχομαι): "praying," modifying the subject (Agamemnon); **θάνατόν** (acc. sg. masc. of θάνατος): "death," object of φυγεῖν; **φυγεῖν** (aor. act. infinitive of φεύγω): "to escape," complementing εὐχόμενος; **μῶλον** (acc. sg. masc. of μῶλος): "toil, struggle," in apposition with θάνατόν; **Ἄρηος** (gen. sg. masc. of Ἄρης): "of Ares," genitive of possession modifying μῶλον. Agamemnon prays to escape death and the struggle
402:
**Iliad** line: "αὐτὰρ ὃ βοῦν ἱέρευσε ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων"

**αὐτάρ** (conjunction): "but, and then" – marks transition to the main action. **βοῦν** (accusative singular of βοῦς): "ox, bull" – the sacrificial victim. **ἱέρευσε** (aorist indicative, 3rd singular of ἱερεύω): "sacrificed, slaughtered for ritual purposes." **ἄναξ** (nominative singular): "lord, king" – formulaic epithet. **Ἀγαμέμνων** (nominative): Agamemnon, the Greek commander, performs the sacrifice.
403: **πίονα** (adj., acc. sing. masc.) "fat, sleek" modifies the bull being sacrificed. **πενταέτηρον** (adj., acc. sing. masc.) "five years old" specifies the age of the sacrificial victim. **ὑπερμενέϊ** (adj., dat. sing. masc.) "exceeding mighty, very powerful" modifies **Κρονίωνι** (noun, dat. sing. masc.) "son of Kronos," referring to Zeus as recipient of the sacrifice. Agamemnon sacrifices a prime five-year-old bull to Zeus.
404: **κίκλησκεν** (impf. act. ind. 3rd sg. of κικλήσκω) "he summoned" or "he was calling"; **γέροντας** (acc. pl. masc. of γέρων) "elders, old men"; **ἀριστῆας** (acc. pl. masc. of ἀριστεύς) "chiefs, best men"; **Παναχαιῶν** (gen. pl. of Πανάχαιοι) "of all the Achaeans." Agamemnon summoned the elder chiefs from among all the Achaeans to a council.
405:
**Νέστορα μὲν πρώτιστα καὶ Ἰδομενῆα ἄνακτα**

Νέστορα (acc. sg. of Νέστωρ): "Nestor," object of κίκλησκεν from previous line. πρώτιστα (adv., superlative of πρῶτος): "first of all," "very first." Ἰδομενῆα (acc. sg. of Ἰδομενεύς): "Idomeneus," Cretan leader, second object. ἄνακτα (acc. sg. of ἄναξ): "lord," "king," in apposition to Ἰδομενῆα. Agamemnon summons the elders, beginning with Nestor first and then lord Idomeneus.
406:
**αὐτὰρ ἔπειτʼ** (adverb + adverb): "but then," "next" - transitional formula marking sequence in the narrative.

**Αἴαντε** (noun, acc. dual, masc.): "the two Ajaxes" - dual form referring to Ajax son of Telamon and Ajax son of Oïleus.

**δύω** (numeral, acc. dual): "two" - emphasizing the pair.

**Τυδέος υἱόν** (noun gen. + noun acc.): "son of Tydeus" - patronymic periphrasis for Diomedes.

The line continues the catalogue of summoned leaders, now naming the two Ajaxes and Diomedes.
407: **ἕκτον** (adjective, accusative singular masculine) "sixth" - ordinal number modifying Odysseus in the sequence of warriors summoned. **Ὀδυσῆα** (proper noun, accusative singular) "Odysseus" - object of an implied verb of summoning. **Διὶ** (proper noun, dative singular) "to Zeus" - dative of comparison. **μῆτιν** (noun, accusative singular feminine) "in counsel/cunning" - accusative of respect. **ἀτάλαντον** (adjective, accusative singular masculine) "equal, comparable" - agreeing with Odysseus, describing him as Zeus's equal in strategic intelligence.
408:
**Key words:** αὐτόματος (nominative singular masculine adjective) "of his own accord, unbidden"; ἦλθε (3rd singular aorist indicative of ἔρχομαι) "came"; βοὴν ἀγαθός (nominative singular masculine, formulaic epithet) "good at the war cry, good in battle," modifying Μενέλαος.

Menelaus, good at the war cry, came to him unbidden/of his own accord (without being summoned).
409:
**ᾔδεε** (pluperfect, 3rd sg. of οἶδα): "he knew"; **κατὰ θυμόν**: "in his heart/mind" (prepositional phrase); **ἀδελφεός** (acc. sg. masc.): "brother"; **ὡς**: "how" (conjunction); **ἐπονεῖτο** (impf. mid./pass., 3rd sg. of πονέομαι): "was toiling/distressed." 

Menelaus intuitively knew in his heart how his brother was laboring or in distress, prompting his spontaneous arrival to help.
410: **βοῦν** (acc. sg. m. of βοῦς) "ox/bull," direct object of περιστήσαντο. **περιστήσαντο** (3rd pl. aor. mid. indic. of περιίστημι) "they stood around," the preparatory ritual action. **οὐλοχύτας** (acc. pl. f. of οὐλοχύτη) "barley grains," ritual grain scattered on the victim. **ἀνέλοντο** (3rd pl. aor. mid. indic. of ἀναιρέω) "they took up/lifted." The line describes the initial sacrificial ritual: they stood around the bull and took up the sacred barley grains to scatter.
411: **τοῖσιν** (dative plural demonstrative pronoun) "among them/to these"; **εὐχόμενος** (present middle participle, nominative singular masculine) "praying, making a vow"; **μετέφη** (3rd singular aorist middle indicative of μεταφημί) "spoke among, addressed"; **κρείων** (nominative singular masculine present participle of κρείω) "ruling, lord"; **Ἀγαμέμνων** (nominative singular) "Agamemnon." Lord Agamemnon spoke among them while praying/making his vow.
412: **Ζεῦ** (vocative of Ζεύς) "Zeus"; **κύδιστε** (vocative superlative adjective) "most glorious"; **μέγιστε** (vocative superlative adjective) "greatest"; **κελαινεφές** (vocative compound adjective, κελαιν- "dark" + νεφ- "cloud") "dark-clouded"; **ναίων** (present active participle, nominative masculine singular of ναίω) "dwelling." An invocation to Zeus with accumulated epithets: the greatest and most glorious god who dwells in the dark-clouded upper air.
413: Key words: **πρίν** (adverb) "before"; **ἠέλιον** (accusative singular of ἠέλιος) "sun," object of ἐπί; **δῦναι** (aorist infinitive of δύω) "to set, go down"; **κνέφας** (accusative singular neuter) "darkness," object of ἐπί; **ἐλθεῖν** (aorist infinitive of ἔρχομαι) "to come." The line means "let not the sun set and darkness come before [I accomplish my goal]," with the doubled ἐπί governing both infinitive clauses.
414: **πρίν** (adv.) "before" governs the infinitives; **κατὰ πρηνὲς** (adv. phrase, neut. acc.) "headlong/forward, prostrate" modifies **βαλέειν** (aor. act. inf. of βάλλω) "to cast down, hurl"; **Πριάμοιο μέλαθρον** (gen. + acc.) "Priam's hall/palace." The speaker vows not to stop before casting Priam's palace headlong (i.e., destroying it completely).
415: **αἰθαλόεν** (acc. sing. masc. participle, *αἰθαλόω*) "blackened with soot, smoke-begrimed" — modifies μέλαθρον from the previous line, describing Priam's palace. **πρῆσαι** (aor. inf., *πίμπρημι*) "to burn, set ablaze" — dependent on an implied verb of necessity or desire. **πυρός** (gen. sing., *πῦρ*) "of fire" — genitive of material. **δηΐοιο** (gen. sing., *δήϊος*) "hostile, destructive" — modifies πυρός. **θύρετρα** (acc. pl. neut., *θύρετρον*) "doorways, gates" — direct object of πρῆσαι.
416: **Ἑκτόρεον** (adjective, masculine accusative singular) "of Hector, Hector's"; **χιτῶνα** (noun, masculine accusative singular) "tunic, corselet"; **στήθεσσι** (noun, neuter dative plural) "upon the chest/breast"; **δαΐξαι** (verb, aorist active infinitive of *δαΐζω*) "to tear, rend, rip apart." The infinitive continues the dependent construction from the previous lines, expressing the speaker's desire to rend Hector's tunic upon his chest.
417: **χαλκῷ** (dative singular, "with bronze"): instrumental dative indicating the weapon. **ῥωγαλέον** (accusative singular adjective, "jagged, torn"): describes the tunic rent by bronze. **πολέες** (nominative plural, "many"): subject describing numerous companions. **ἑταῖροι** (nominative plural, "companions"): Hector's comrades who surround and protect him. The line depicts Hector's torn tunic and the protective circle of his many comrades around him.
418: **πρηνέες** (adj. nom. pl. masc.): "face-forward, headlong," describing the fallen companions. **κονίῃσιν** (noun dat. pl. fem.): "in the dust," from κονίη. **ὀδάξ** (adv.): "with the teeth, biting," intensifying the image of death. **λαζοίατο** (verb 3rd pl. aor. mid. opt.): "might seize, bite," from λάζομαι. **γαῖαν** (noun acc. sg. fem.): "the earth, ground." The companions lie headlong in the dust, biting the earth in death—a vivid Homeric formula for violent death in battle.
419:
**ὣς** (adverb): "thus, so" – marks the conclusion of Agamemnon's prayer.

**ἔφατʼ** (3rd sg. impf. mid., φημί): "he spoke" – refers to Agamemnon's prayer just completed.

**ἐπεκραίαινε** (3rd sg. impf. act., ἐπικραιαίνω): "was fulfilling, was granting" – the negated verb indicates Zeus's refusal.

**Κρονίων** (nom. sg. masc., Κρονίων): "son of Kronos, Zeus" – the subject who does not yet grant the prayer.

The line marks the tragic irony: Agamemnon spoke thus, but the son of Kronos was not yet fulfilling his prayer for him.
420:
**Key words:** δέκτο (3rd sg. impf. mid. δέχομαι) "he received"; ἱρά (n. pl. acc. ἱερόν) "sacrifices, offerings"; πόνον (m. sg. acc. πόνος) "toil, suffering"; ἀμέγαρτον (m. sg. acc. ἀμέγαρτος) "unenvied, grievous"; ὄφελλεν (3rd sg. impf. ὀφέλλω) "he was heaping up, increasing."

The verse depicts Zeus accepting the sacrifices but simultaneously increasing grievous suffering—the contrast between μέν and δέ emphasizes the ironic disparity between receiving worship and granting disaster.
421:
**Key words:** εὔξαντο (aorist middle, 3rd pl. of εὔχομαι, "they prayed"), οὐλοχύτας (acc. pl. of οὐλοχύται, "barley grains" for ritual sprinkling), προβάλοντο (aorist middle, 3rd pl. of προβάλλω, "they threw forward/scattered"). 

**Gloss:** This line describes the preliminary ritual actions of sacrifice: after they prayed and scattered the barley grains (a standard opening to Greek animal sacrifice), the next verse will detail the actual slaughter.
422: **αὐέρυσαν** (ἀνερύω, 3rd pl. aor. indic. act.) "they drew back [the victims' heads]"; **πρῶτα** (adv.) "first"; **ἔσφαξαν** (σφάζω, 3rd pl. aor. indic. act.) "they slaughtered"; **ἔδειραν** (δέρω, 3rd pl. aor. indic. act.) "they flayed." This line describes the initial stages of sacrificial ritual: drawing back the victims' heads, slaughtering them, and flaying the carcasses, with **μέν** anticipating a subsequent step in the procedure.
423:
**μηρούς** (acc. pl. masc. of μηρός): thighs, the portions cut for the gods. **ἐξέταμον** (3rd pl. aor. act. indic. of ἐκτέμνω): they cut out. **κατά** (tmesis with ἐκάλυψαν): over, upon. **κνίσῃ** (dat. sg. fem. of κνίσα/κνίση): fat. **ἐκάλυψαν** (3rd pl. aor. act. indic. of καλύπτω): they covered.

They cut out the thigh-bones and covered them over with fat, the standard ritual preparation for burning portions offered to the gods.
424: **δίπτυχα** (adj. acc. pl. neut.) "double-folded," modifying an understood object (the thigh pieces); **ποιήσαντες** (aor. act. ptc. nom. pl. masc. from ποιέω) "having made"; **ἐπ' αὐτῶν** (prep. + gen. pl.) "upon them"; **ὠμοθέτησαν** (aor. act. ind. 3rd pl. from ὠμοθετέω) "they placed raw flesh." Having made the thigh pieces double-folded, they placed raw meat upon them before burning.
425:
**καὶ τὰ μὲν ἂρ σχίζῃσιν ἀφύλλοισιν κατέκαιον:**

**τὰ** (neuter plural accusative, demonstrative pronoun): "these things," referring to the thigh pieces wrapped in fat; **σχίζῃσιν** (dative plural, from σχίζα): "on split wood" or "on spits/kindling"; **ἀφύλλοισιν** (dative plural adjective, from ἄφυλλος): "leafless," modifying σχίζῃσιν; **κατέκαιον** (3rd plural imperfect active, from κατακαίω): "they were burning" or "they burned up/consumed." The line describes the ritual burning of the thigh bones wrapped in fat on stripped sticks during
426: **σπλάγχνα** (neuter accusative plural, "inner organs, entrails") is the direct object of **ἀμπείραντες** (aorist active participle, nominative plural masculine, from ἀναπείρω, "having pierced through, having spitted"). **ὑπείρεχον** (imperfect active, 3rd plural, from ὑπερέχω, "they held over") describes how they held the spitted organs over **Ἡφαίστοιο** (genitive singular, "of Hephaestus," i.e., the fire). The line depicts the ritual roasting of sacrificial organs after burning the thigh-pieces.
427: **αὐτὰρ** (particle) "but, and then" marks transition to next stage of sacrifice. **κατὰ ... κάη** (κατακαίω, aor. pass. 3rd sg.) "were burned down/consumed," describing the thighbones burned on altar. **μῆρε** (μηρός, acc. dual) "thighbones," the portions offered to gods. **σπλάγχνα** (σπλάγχνον, acc. pl. neut.) "inner organs, entrails." **πάσαντο** (πατέομαι, aor. mid. 3rd pl.) "they tasted, partook of," referring to ritual tasting of roasted organs.
428:
**μίστυλλον** (3rd pl. impf. act. indic. of μιστυλλέω): "they cut up (the meat into small pieces)"; **τἆλλα** (= τὰ ἄλλα, acc. pl. neut. of ἄλλος): "the rest, the remaining parts"; **ὀβελοῖσιν** (dat. pl. of ὀβελός): "on/with spits"; **ἔπειραν** (3rd pl. aor. act. indic. of πείρω): "they pierced, threaded."

After the thigh pieces burned and they tasted the entrails, they cut up the remaining meat and pierced it onto spits in preparation for roasting.
429: **ὤπτησαν** (ὀπτάω, 3rd pl. aor. act. indic.) "they roasted"; **περιφραδέως** (adv.) "skillfully, with care"; **ἐρύσαντο** (ἐρύω, 3rd pl. aor. mid. indic.) "they drew off, pulled [from the spits]"; **πάντα** (πᾶς, neut. acc. pl., substantive) "all things, everything." The line describes the completion of roasting the meat carefully and removing it all from the spits.
430: **αὐτὰρ** (particle): "but, and then" (transitional conjunction). **ἐπεὶ** (conjunction): "when, after" (+ aorist). **παύσαντο** (verb): 3rd pl. aorist middle indicative of παύω, "they ceased, stopped" (from labor). **τετύκοντο** (verb): 3rd pl. pluperfect middle indicative of τεύχω, "they had prepared, made ready." The line marks the transition from food preparation to feasting: after they stopped their labor and had prepared the meal.
431:
**δαίνυντʼ** (δαίνυνται, 3rd pl. impf. mid., "they feasted"); **θυμός** (nom. sg., "heart, spirit"); **ἐδεύετο** (3rd sg. impf. mid. of δεύομαι, "lacked, wanted"); **δαιτός** (gen. sg. fem., "feast, banquet"); **ἐΐσης** (gen. sg. fem. of ἐΐσος, "equal, fair"). 

They feasted, and no one's heart lacked anything of the equal/well-shared banquet—a typical Homeric formula indicating satisfying hospitality where all received proper portions.
432: **ἐπεί** (conjunction) "when, after"; **πόσιος** (gen. sg. of πόσις) "of drink"; **ἐδητύος** (gen. sg. of ἐδητύς) "of food"; **ἔρον** (acc. sg. of ἔρος) "desire, appetite"; **ἕντο** (3rd pl. aor. mid. of ἵημι) "they satisfied, put from themselves." The line marks the transition from feasting to speech: "But when they had satisfied their desire for food and drink."
433:
**Key words:** τοῖς (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural, "to them/among them"), ἦρχε (verb, 3rd singular imperfect active indicative of ἄρχω, "began"), Γερήνιος (adjective, nominative singular masculine, "Gerenian," epithet of Nestor), ἱππότα (noun, nominative singular masculine, "horseman/knight," epithet), Νέστωρ (proper noun, nominative singular, "Nestor"). 

Among them Gerenian Nestor the horseman began his speech; the imperfect ἦρχε introduces Nestor's direct address.
434: **Ἀτρεΐδη** (vocative singular, "son of Atreus"), **κύδιστε** (vocative singular superlative adjective, "most glorious"), **ἄναξ** (vocative singular noun, "lord, king"), **ἀνδρῶν** (genitive plural, "of men"), **Ἀγάμεμνον** (vocative, "Agamemnon"). This is a formal address to Agamemnon using traditional epic epithets: "Son of Atreus, most glorious lord of men, Agamemnon."
435:
**μηκέτι** (adverb): "no longer," negating further delay. **νῦν** (adverb): "now," emphasizing immediate action. **δήθ(α)** (adverb): "for a long time," reinforcing the prohibition of lingering. **λεγώμεθα** (1st pl. pres. middle subjunctive, λέγω): "let us gather/converse," hortatory subjunctive negated to mean "let us not delay in gathering/talking." **δηρόν** (adverb, accusative of duration): "for a long time," further emphasizing avoidance of protracted delay.

The speaker urges immediate action, rejecting any further postponement through deliberation or assembly.
436: **ἀμβαλλώμεθα** (1st pl. pres. mid. subj. of ἀναβάλλω) "let us postpone"; **ἔργον** (acc. sg. neut. noun) "the task, work"; **θεός** (nom. sg. masc. noun) "god, the god"; **ἐγγυαλίζει** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of ἐγγυαλίζω) "entrusts, puts into (our) hands." Hector urges the Trojans not to delay the task/battle that god now places before them, creating urgency for immediate action rather than continued deliberation.
437: **ἀλλʼ ἄγε** (ἀλλά + ἄγε): "but come!" - standard exhortation introducing a command. **κήρυκες** (nom. pl. of κῆρυξ): "heralds" - subject of implied verb. **Ἀχαιῶν** (gen. pl. of Ἀχαιός): "of the Achaeans" - possessive genitive modifying heralds. **χαλκοχιτώνων** (gen. pl. adj. from χαλκοχίτων): "bronze-clad" - compound epithet (χαλκός + χιτών) modifying Achaeans, describing their bronze armor.
438:
**λαὸν** (acc. sing. masc., "people/host") — the object of the heralds' gathering activity. **κηρύσσοντες** (pres. part. nom. pl. masc., "proclaiming/making proclamation") — describes the heralds' activity as they gather the troops. **ἀγειρόντων** (3rd pl. pres. impv., "let them gather") — imperative directing the heralds to assemble the army. **νῆας** (acc. pl. fem., "ships") — locative destination, where the gathering occurs.

The line commands that the heralds gather the host by making proclamation throughout the camp near the ships.
439:
**ἡμεῖς** (pronoun, nom. pl.) "we" – subject emphasizing the leaders' collective action in contrast to the heralds. **ἀθρόοι** (adj., nom. pl. masc.) "gathered together, in a body" – predicative, describing their unified movement. **κατὰ στρατόν** (prep. + acc.) "throughout the army" – indicating distribution across the camp. **εὐρύν** (adj., acc. sg. masc.) "wide, broad" – modifying στρατόν, emphasizing the army's extent. 

The leaders will move collectively throughout the broad Achaean army while the heralds summon the troops.
440:
**ἴομεν** (1st pl. pres. subj. of εἶμι) "let us go"; **ὄφρα** (conj.) "so that, in order that"; **θᾶσσον** (comparative adv. from ταχύς) "more quickly, swiftly"; **ἐγείρομεν** (1st pl. pres. subj. of ἐγείρω) "we may rouse, stir up"; **ὀξὺν Ἄρηα** (acc. sg., "sharp/keen Ares") metonymy for battle or war. 

The speaker urges the assembled Achaean army to proceed together in order to more swiftly kindle fierce battle.
441:
**ὣς ἔφατʼ, οὐδʼ ἀπίθησεν ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων.**

Key words: **ἔφατο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of φημί, "he spoke"), **ἀπίθησεν** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of ἀπιθέω, "disobeyed," here negated by οὐδέ), **ἄναξ** (nom. sg. masc., "lord, king"), **ἀνδρῶν** (gen. pl. of ἀνήρ, "of men"). Thus he spoke, and the lord of men Agamemnon did not disobey.
442: **αὐτίκα** (adv.): immediately, at once. **κηρύκεσσι** (dat. pl. of κῆρυξ): to the heralds. **λιγυφθόγγοισι** (adj. dat. pl., modifying κηρύκεσσι): clear-voiced, loud-voiced. **κέλευσε** (3rd sg. aor. ind. act. of κελεύω): he commanded, ordered. Agamemnon immediately commanded the clear-voiced heralds to summon the long-haired Achaeans to war.
443: κηρύσσειν (present infinitive of κηρύσσω, "to proclaim") depends on κέλευσε from the previous line. πόλεμον (accusative singular masculine of πόλεμος, "war") is the object of κηρύσσειν. κάρη κομόωντας (accusative plural masculine present participle of κομάω, "wearing long hair") modifies Ἀχαιούς (accusative plural of Ἀχαιοί, "the Achaeans"), creating the traditional epithet "long-haired Achaeans." The infinitive construction completes Agamemnon's command to the heralds to summon the Greeks to war.
444:
**οἳ** (hoi): demonstrative pronoun, nominative plural masculine, "these men" (the heralds).

**ἐκήρυσσον** (ekērysson): imperfect active 3rd plural of κηρύσσω, "were proclaiming/announcing" (the call to war).

**ἠγείροντο** (ēgeironto): imperfect middle/passive 3rd plural of ἐγείρω, "were gathering/being roused."

**μάλʼ ὦκα** (mal' ōka): adverbial phrase, "very swiftly/quickly" (elided μάλα + ὦκα).

The line contrasts the heralds' proclamation with the Achaeans' swift response to assemble.
445:
**οἳ** (demonstrative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "they" — δέ (postpositive particle) "and, but" — **ἀμφʼ** (preposition + acc., elided from ἀμφί) "around" — **Ἀτρεΐωνα** (acc. sg. masc., patronymic) "the son of Atreus" [Agamemnon] — **διοτρεφέες** (adj., nom. pl. masc.) "Zeus-nurtured, divinely fostered" — **βασιλῆες** (noun, nom. pl. masc.) "kings, chieftains." 

The chieftains gather around Agamemnon, contrasting with the general assembly being marshaled.
446: **θῦνον** (imperfect, 3rd pl. of θύνω): "were rushing about" or "were moving busily." **κρίνοντες** (pres. act. participle, nom. pl. masc. of κρίνω): "marshaling" or "arranging" (the troops). **μετὰ** (preposition + acc.): "among" (them). **γλαυκῶπις** (nom. sg. fem. epithet): "gray-eyed" or "bright-eyed." **Ἀθήνη** (nom. sg. fem.): "Athena." The kings rush about marshaling their forces, with gray-eyed Athena moving among them.
447: **αἰγίδα** (accusative singular feminine of αἰγίς): "aegis," the divine shield or breastplate of Athena. **ἔχουσα** (present active participle, nominative singular feminine of ἔχω): "holding" or "bearing." **ἐρίτιμον** (accusative singular feminine of ἐρίτιμος): "very precious" or "highly honored." **ἀγήρων** (accusative singular feminine of ἀγήρως): "ageless." **ἀθανάτην** (accusative singular feminine of ἀθάνατος): "immortal." Athena holds her aegis, described with three emphatic epithets emphasizing its divine, eternal nature as both precious and imperishable.
448:
**τῆς** (genitive singular feminine of ὁ ἡ τό): "of it/from it," referring to the aegis. **ἑκατόν** (indeclinable numeral): "hundred." **θύσανοι** (nominative plural masculine of θύσανος): "tassels, fringes." **παγχρύσεοι** (nominative plural masculine of παγχρύσεος): "all-golden, entirely of gold." **ἠερέθονται** (3rd plural present passive of ἠερέθομαι): "are suspended, hang down."

From the aegis a hundred all-golden tassels hang suspended, describing the ornate decoration of Athena's divine armor.
449: **πάντες** (πᾶς, nom. masc. pl.): "all," agreeing with θύσανοι from the previous line. **ἐϋπλεκέες** (ἐϋπλεκής, nom. masc. pl.): "well-plaited, finely woven," describing the tassels. **ἑκατόμβοιος** (ἑκατόμβοιος, gen. fem. sg.): "worth a hundred oxen," genitive of value modifying the following noun. **ἕκαστος** (ἕκαστος, nom. masc. sg.): "each one," emphasizing the individual value of each tassel. The line continues the description of Athena's aegis, noting that all the tassels are finely crafted and each is worth a hecatomb.
450:
**Key words:** σὺν τῇ (preposition + dative pronoun, "with her/it"), παιφάσσουσα (present participle nominative feminine singular from παιφάσσω, "flashing/glancing"), διέσσυτο (3rd singular aorist middle indicative from *διασεύομαι*, "rushed through/darted through"), λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν (accusative singular λαός + genitive plural, "the host of the Achaeans"). 

Athena, flashing with her aegis, rushed through the Achaean army, rousing each warrior's strength for battle.
451:
**ὀτρύνουσʼ ἰέναι· ἐν δὲ σθένος ὦρσεν ἑκάστῳ**

**ὀτρύνουσα** (pres. act. participle, nom. fem. sg. of ὀτρύνω): "urging, rousing"
**ἰέναι** (pres. inf. of εἶμι): "to go"
**σθένος** (noun, acc. neut. sg.): "strength, might"
**ὦρσεν** (aor. act. ind. 3rd sg. of ὄρνυμι): "she stirred up, roused"
**ἑκάστῳ** (adj./pron., dat. masc. sg.): "to each (man)"

Ath
452: **καρδίῃ** (dat. sing. fem. of καρδία): "in heart/spirit," dative of respect or location. **ἄλληκτον** (acc. sing. neut. of ἄλληκτος): "unceasingly, without pause," adverbial accusative modifying the infinitives. **πολεμίζειν** (pres. act. inf. of πολεμίζω): "to wage war." **μάχεσθαι** (pres. mid. inf. of μάχομαι): "to fight." The line describes their unwavering spirit to fight continuously, with complementary infinitives expressing the action they desire in their hearts.
453:
**τοῖσι** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural): "for them/these men"
**ἄφαρ** (adverb): "straightaway, immediately"
**γλυκίων** (comparative adjective, nominative singular masculine): "sweeter," from γλυκύς
**γένετο** (verb, 3rd singular aorist middle indicative of γίγνομαι): "became"
**νέεσθαι** (verb, present middle infinitive of νέομαι): "to return (home)"

For these men, war immediately became sweeter than returning home, contrasting the goddess-induced battle-lust with the prospect of sailing back to their fatherland.
454: **νηυσὶ** (noun, dative plural of ναῦς): "in ships," dative of place where or means. **γλαφυρῇσι** (adjective, dative plural feminine of γλαφυρός): "hollow, curved," modifying νηυσί. **φίλην** (adjective, accusative singular feminine of φίλος): "dear, beloved," modifying πατρίδα γαῖαν. **πατρίδα** (adjective, accusative singular feminine of πατρίς): "fatherland, native," with γαῖαν forming "native land." The line describes returning home in their hollow ships to their dear fatherland.
455:
**ἠΰτε πῦρ ἀΐδηλον ἐπιφλέγει ἄσπετον ὕλην**

**ἠΰτε** (conjunction): "just as," introduces epic simile comparing the gleam of weapons to fire. **πῦρ** (neuter nominative singular): "fire," subject of the simile. **ἀΐδηλον** (adjective, nominative neuter singular): "destructive, devouring," modifying πῦρ. **ἐπιφλέγει** (3rd singular present indicative): "blazes up, kindles," from ἐπιφλέγω. **ἄσπετον** (adjective, accusative feminine singular): "unspeakable, immense," modifying ὕλην. **ὕλην** (accusative
456:
**Key words:** *οὔρεος* (gen. sg. of ὄρος) "of a mountain"; *κορυφῇς* (dat. pl. of κορυφή) "on the peaks"; *ἕκαθεν* (adv.) "from afar"; *φαίνεται* (3rd sg. pres. mid./pass. of φαίνω) "is seen, appears"; *αὐγή* (nom. sg.) "gleam, light."

The simile continues: the fire blazes on the mountain peaks, and from afar the gleam is visible—establishing the visual magnitude of the bronze armor's brightness across the moving Greek army.
457: **ὣς** (adverb): thus, so; introduces the comparison's application. **τῶν ἐρχομένων** (genitive plural masculine present participle of ἔρχομαι): "of them going/marching," referring to the advancing warriors. **ἀπὸ χαλκοῦ** (preposition + genitive singular): "from the bronze," indicating the source of the gleam from their armor. **θεσπεσίοιο** (genitive singular adjective): "wondrous, marvelous, god-sent," modifying χαλκοῦ and emphasizing the divine quality of their bronze equipment.
458:
**αἴγλη** (nom. sg. fem., "gleam, radiance") **παμφανόωσα** (pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. fem. from παμφανάω, "shining all around, flashing brightly") **διʼ** (prep. + gen., δια with elision, "through") **αἰθέρος** (gen. sg. masc., "upper air, sky") **οὐρανὸν** (acc. sg. masc., "heaven, sky") **ἷκε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. from ἱκνέομαι, "reached, came to"). 

The gleaming radiance, flashing all around, reached through the upper air to heaven—describing the brilliant light reflecting from the bronze armor of the advancing warriors.
459:
**τῶν** (demonstrative pronoun, genitive plural) "of them"; **ὀρνίθων** (noun, genitive plural from ὄρνις) "of birds"; **πετεηνῶν** (adjective, genitive plural from πετεηνός) "winged, flying"; **ἔθνεα** (noun, nominative/accusative plural from ἔθνος) "tribes, flocks"; **πολλά** (adjective, nominative/accusative plural neuter) "many." 

The line introduces a simile comparing the multitudes of warriors to many flocks of winged birds, with the genitive construction specifying "flocks of flying birds."
460:
**χηνῶν** (genitive plural of χήν): "of geese"; **γεράνων** (genitive plural of γέρανος): "of cranes"; **κύκνων** (genitive plural of κύκνος): "of swans"; **δουλιχοδείρων** (genitive plural adjective, modifying κύκνων): "long-necked." 

The line catalogs three types of waterfowl in genitive partitive construction, completing the simile comparing the numerous Greek tribes to flocks of birds; the compound epithet δουλιχοδείρων ("long-necked") applies specifically to the swans.
461:
**Ἀσίω ἐν λειμῶνι Καϋστρίου ἀμφὶ ῥέεθρα**

*Ἀσίω* (adj. dat. sg. neut.): "Asian," modifying *λειμῶνι*. *λειμῶνι* (noun dat. sg. masc.): "in the meadow," locative dative. *Καϋστρίου* (proper name gen. sg.): "of the Cayster," a river in Asia Minor near Ephesus. *ἀμφὴ* (prep. + acc.): "around, near." *ῥέεθρα* (noun acc. pl. neut.): "streams, waters." The birds settle around the flowing waters of the Cayster River in the Asian meadow.
462: **ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα** (adverb): "hither and thither," "in one direction and another"—a formulaic phrase indicating movement in all directions. **ποτῶνται** (3rd pl. pres. mid./pass. indic. of *ποτάομαι*): "they fly about," describing the birds' flight. **ἀγαλλόμενα** (nom./acc. pl. neut. pres. mid. participle of *ἀγάλλομαι*): "exulting," "glorying," modifying the birds in their joyful display. **πτερύγεσσι** (dat. pl. of *πτέρυξ*): "in their wings," instrumental dative expressing the means of their exultation.
463: **κλαγγηδόν** (adverb): "with clamor/din," describing the noisy settling down of the troops. **προκαθιζόντων** (present participle, genitive plural masculine from προκαθίζω): "of those sitting/settling down before," genitive absolute construction. **σμαραγεῖ** (present indicative, 3rd singular from σμαραγέω): "roars/resounds," the meadow echoes with sound. **λειμών** (nominative singular masculine): "meadow/plain," subject of the verb, the field where the troops gather.
464:
**ὣς** (adverb): "thus, so" – drawing the simile's comparison between birds and Greek forces.

**ἔθνεα** (noun, nominative plural, neuter): "tribes, companies, bands" – the organized contingents of Greek warriors.

**νεῶν** (noun, genitive plural, feminine): "from the ships" – the beached Greek fleet at Troy.

**κλισιάων** (noun, genitive plural, feminine): "huts, barracks" – the temporary shelters of the Greek camp.

The countless Greek companies poured forth from their ships and encampments onto the plain.
465:
**ἐς πεδίον προχέοντο Σκαμάνδριον· αὐτὰρ ὑπὸ χθὼν**

*προχέοντο* (imperfect middle/passive, 3rd plural of προχέω): "poured forth" or "streamed forth," describing the massed movement of troops. *πεδίον* (accusative singular neuter noun): "plain," the destination of motion with *ἐς*. *Σκαμάνδριον* (accusative singular adjective): "Scamandrian," modifying *πεδίον* and referring to the plain near the river Scamander. *χθὼν* (nominative singular feminine noun): "earth" or "ground," subject of the next clause introduced by *αὐτάρ*.
466: **σμερδαλέον** (adverb, "terribly, dreadfully") **κονάβιζε** (3rd sg. impf. act. indic. of κοναβίζω, "resounded, thundered") **ποδῶν** (gen. pl. of πούς, "of feet") **ἵππων** (gen. pl. of ἵππος, "of horses"). The earth resounded terribly beneath the feet of both the men themselves and their horses as they poured forth across the plain.
467: **ἔσταν** (3rd pl. aorist indicative of ἵστημι) "they stood"; **λειμῶνι** (dative singular masculine of λειμών) "in the meadow"; **Σκαμανδρίῳ** (dative singular adjective modifying λειμῶνι) "of Scamander," referring to the Trojan river; **ἀνθεμόεντι** (dative singular adjective) "flowery, blooming." The Achaean forces took their stand in the flowery meadow along the Scamander river.
468: **μυρίοι** (adjective, nominative plural masculine) "countless, numberless"; **φύλλα** (noun, nominative plural neuter) "leaves"; **ἄνθεα** (noun, nominative plural neuter) "flowers"; **γίγνεται** (verb, 3rd singular present middle/passive) "come into being, are born"; **ὥρῃ** (noun, dative singular feminine) "in season, in springtime." The verse uses a double simile comparing the countless Achaean troops to leaves and flowers that bloom in their season.
469: **ἠΰτε** (comparative particle) "just as"; **μυιάων** (genitive plural of μυῖα) "of flies"; **ἁδινάων** (genitive plural adjective) "swarming, clustering"; **ἔθνεα** (nominative/accusative plural neuter of ἔθνος) "swarms, tribes"; **πολλὰ** (nominative/accusative plural neuter adjective) "many." The simile compares the multitude of warriors to many swarms of clustering flies, emphasizing their dense numbers.
470: **αἵ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. fem.) "which" – refers back to the swarms of flies; **κατά** (preposition + acc.) "throughout, around"; **σταθμόν** (acc. sg. masc.) "farmstead, stable" – the shepherds' dwelling; **ποιμνήϊον** (adj. acc. sg. masc.) "of the flocks, pastoral" – modifies σταθμόν; **ἠλάσκουσιν** (3rd pl. pres. indic.) "buzz about, dart around" – iterative verb describing the flies' swarming motion around the pastoral buildings.
471:
**ὥρῃ** (dat. sg. fem. of ὥρη): "in the season," temporal dative indicating when the action occurs.
**εἰαρινῇ** (dat. sg. fem. of εἰαρινός): "of spring," adjective modifying ὥρῃ.
**γλάγος** (nom. sg. neut. of γλάγος): "milk," subject of the verb, referring to fresh milk from ewes.
**ἄγγεα** (acc. pl. neut. of ἄγγος): "pails" or "vessels," direct object, containers for the milk.
**δεύει** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of δεύω): "wets" or "moistens," describing how the abundant milk fills the vessels. This simile elaborates the pastoral comparison, depicting the springtime abundance
472: **τόσσοι** (demonstrative pronoun, nominative plural masculine): "so many," correlating with the preceding simile. **ἐπί** (preposition + dative): "against" (with hostile sense). **Τρώεσσι** (noun, dative plural): "the Trojans," indicating the target of the Achaeans' advance. **κάρη κομόωντες** (noun + participle, nominative plural masculine): "long-haired," literally "wearing their hair on their heads," a traditional Homeric epithet. **Ἀχαιοί** (noun, nominative plural): "the Achaeans," subject of the sentence in the following line.
473:
**ἐν πεδίῳ** (preposition + dative neuter singular of πεδίον): "in the plain"
**ἵσταντο** (3rd plural imperfect middle-passive indicative of ἵστημι): "stood, took their stand"
**διαρραῖσαι** (aorist active infinitive of διαρραίω): "to break through, to shatter"
**μεμαῶτες** (nominative masculine plural perfect active participle of μέμονα): "eager, striving"

The long-haired Achaeans stood arrayed in the plain, eager to break through (the Trojan lines).
474:
**Key words:** αἰπόλια (nom. pl. neut., "herds of goats"), αἰγῶν (gen. pl. fem., "of goats"), αἰπόλοι (nom. pl. masc., "goatherds"), ἄνδρες (nom. pl. masc., "men"), πλατέα (acc. pl. neut., "wide-ranging, scattered").

The leaders organize their troops just as goatherd men easily separate wide-ranging herds of goats; the simile continues the pastoral comparison begun in the previous lines.
475: **ῥεῖα** (adverb): "easily," modifying the verb διακρίνωσιν. **διακρίνωσιν** (3rd pl. aor. subj. act. of διακρίνω): "they separate," referring to the shepherds sorting their flocks. **ἐπεί κε** (temporal conjunction + modal particle): "whenever," introducing a temporal clause. **νομῷ** (dat. sg. of νομός): "in/at pasture," locative dative indicating where the mixing occurs. **μιγέωσιν** (3rd pl. aor. subj. pass. of μίγνυμι): "they have become mixed," describing the goats mingling together.
476:
**ὣς** (adverb): "thus, so" — marks the transition back to the main narrative after the simile.

**ἡγεμόνες** (noun, nominative plural): "leaders, commanders" — the Greek chieftains organizing their troops.

**διεκόσμεον** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect active): "were marshaling, were arranging in order" — iterative action of organizing the troops for battle.

**ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα** (adverbial phrase): "here and there, in every direction" — emphasizes the commanders' activity throughout the ranks.
