The verse concludes the shepherd simile, describing how the Greek leaders marshaled their forces in all directions, just as shepherds easily separate their mingled flocks.
477:
**ὑσμίνην δʼ ἰέναι, μετὰ δὲ κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων**

*ὑσμίνην* (acc. sing., "battle," "combat") is the object of the infinitive *ἰέναι* (pres. inf. of εἶμι, "to go"). *κρείων* (nom. sing. masc., "lordly," "powerful") modifies *Ἀγαμέμνον* (nom. sing.), and *μετὰ* here functions as an adverb meaning "among them" or "in their midst." The line describes the marshaling into battle with lordly Agamemnon prominent among the troops.
478:
**ὄμματα καὶ κεφαλὴν ἴκελος Διὶ τερπικεραύνῳ**

ὄμματα (nom. pl. neut., ὄμμα): "eyes"; καὶ κεφαλὴν (acc. sg. fem., κεφαλή): "and head"; ἴκελος (nom. sg. masc., ἴκελος): "like, resembling" (+ dat.); Διὶ (dat. sg., Ζεύς): "to Zeus"; τερπικεραύνῳ (dat. sg. masc., τερπικέραυνος): "who delights in thunder/lightning." In respect to his eyes and head, Agamemnon resembles Zeus who delights in the thunderbolt—a comparison emphasizing his commanding,
479: **Ἄρεϊ** (dat. sg., Ἄρης): "to Ares," dative of comparison or likeness. **ζώνην** (acc. sg., ζώνη): "waist/belt," direct object. **στέρνον** (acc. sg., στέρνον): "chest/breast," direct object in the second clause. **Ποσειδάωνι** (dat. sg., Ποσειδάων): "to Poseidon," dative of comparison. The line continues the heroic comparison, with Agamemnon's waist like Ares and chest like Poseidon, emphasizing his martial prowess and physical majesty through divine parallels.
480:
**ἠΰτε** (conjunction): "just as," introduces a simile comparing the subject to a bull among cattle.

**βοῦς** (noun, nominative singular masculine): "bull," subject of the simile.

**ἀγέληφι** (noun, dative singular feminine): "in/among the herd," locative dative indicating position within the group.

**μέγʼ ἔξοχος** (adverb + adjective): "greatly preeminent/outstanding," μέγα (elided) intensifies ἔξοχος (nominative singular), modifying βοῦς.

The line presents a heroic simile: "just as a bull stands out greatly preeminent among all in the herd."
481:
**ταῦρος·** (nom. sg. masc.) "bull" – the subject completing the simile from the previous line.

**μεταπρέπει** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of μεταπρέπω) "stands out among" – the verb describing the bull's pre-eminence.

**βόεσσι** (dat. pl. fem. of βοῦς) "among cattle" – dative of comparison.

**ἀγρομένῃσι** (dat. pl. fem. pres. mid. participle of ἀγείρω) "when gathered together" – modifying the cattle as they are assembled in a herd.

The line completes the simile: the bull stands out conspicuously among the assembled cattle, just as Agamemnon stands pre-eminent among the warriors.
482: **τοῖον** (demonstrative pronoun, accusative singular masculine) "such a one"; **Ἀτρεΐδην** (patronymic noun, accusative singular) "son of Atreus" (referring to Agamemnon); **θῆκε** (aorist active indicative, 3rd singular of τίθημι) "made"; **Ζεύς** (nominative singular) "Zeus"; **ἤματι κείνῳ** (dative singular noun + demonstrative) "on that day." Zeus made the son of Atreus such a one on that day—connecting the simile of the preeminent bull to Agamemnon's distinction among heroes.
483: **ἐκπρεπέα** (adj. acc. sg. masc., "conspicuous, outstanding") and **ἔξοχον** (adj. acc. sg. masc., "preeminent, surpassing") modify the Atreïd from the previous line, describing Zeus's elevation of him. **πολλοῖσι** (adj. dat. pl. masc., "many") and **ἡρώεσσιν** (noun dat. pl., "heroes") form a dative of comparison: "conspicuous among many and preeminent among heroes."
484: **ἔσπετε** (2nd pl. aorist imperative of *ἐνέπω*) "tell!": the poet invokes the Muses to relate the catalog of ships. **Μοῦσαι** (nom. pl., vocative function) "Muses": the goddesses of poetic inspiration addressed directly. **Ὀλύμπια δώματʼ ἔχουσαι** (pres. act. participle, fem. nom. pl. of *ἔχω* + acc. pl. *δώματα*) "who hold/dwell in Olympian halls": identifies the Muses by their divine abode. The invocation marks the transition to the great catalog, emphasizing that only divine knowledge can encompass all the Greek forces.
485: **ὑμεῖς** (pronoun, nom. pl., "you") emphasizes the Muses as opposed to mortals; **θεαί** (noun, nom. pl., "goddesses") identifies their divine nature; **πάρεστέ** (verb, 2nd pl. pres. indic. of πάρειμι, "you are present") stresses their direct witnessing of events; **ἴστέ** (verb, 2nd pl. perf. indic. of οἶδα, "you know") indicates their complete knowledge; **πάντα** (adj., acc. pl. neut., "all things") encompasses their total awareness. The threefold assertion (you are goddesses, are present, know all) contrasts the Muses' omniscience with mortal limitation expressed in the following line.
486: **ἡμεῖς** (pronoun, nom. pl., "we") contrasts mortals with the goddesses; **κλέος** (noun, acc. sg., "fame/report") is the indirect object of hearing; **οἶον** (adverb, "only/alone") emphasizes the limitation; **ἀκούομεν** (verb, 1st pl. pres. indic., "we hear") and **ἴδμεν** (verb, 1st pl. perf. indic. with pres. meaning, "we know") form a contrastive pair. The line stresses human dependence on hearsay versus divine omniscience.
487:
**οἵ τινες ἡγεμόνες Δαναῶν καὶ κοίρανοι ἦσαν·**

**οἵ τινες** (relative pronoun, nominative plural masculine) "who(ever), which ones"; **ἡγεμόνες** (noun, nominative plural) "leaders, commanders"; **Δαναῶν** (noun, genitive plural) "of the Danaans/Greeks"; **κοίρανοι** (noun, nominative plural) "chiefs, lords"; **ἦσαν** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect) "were." The poet introduces the Catalogue of Ships by identifying which Greek leaders and chiefs he will enumerate.
488: **πληθύν** (accusative singular feminine of πληθύς): "multitude, mass" — the countless throng of warriors. **μυθήσομαι** (1st singular future middle indicative of μυθέομαι): "I shall recount, tell of." **ὀνομήνω** (1st singular aorist subjunctive of ὀνομαίνω): "I could name, enumerate." The poet declares his inability to recount or name the multitude even if he tried (**οὐκ ἄν** with subjunctive expressing potential negation).
489:
**Key words:** *δέκα* (numeral, indeclinable) "ten"; *γλῶσσαι* (noun, nom. pl. fem. from γλῶσσα) "tongues"; *στόματα* (noun, nom. pl. neut. from στόμα) "mouths"; *εἶεν* (verb, 3rd pl. pres. opt. from εἰμί) "were, would be."

The poet employs a contrary-to-fact condition to emphasize impossibility: not even if he possessed ten tongues and ten mouths could he enumerate the Greek host.
490:
**φωνὴ** (noun, nominative singular feminine) "voice" – subject of the implied verb "were." **ἄρρηκτος** (adjective, nominative singular feminine) "unbreakable, tireless" from ἀ-privative + ῥήγνυμι, modifying φωνή. **χάλκεον** (adjective, nominative singular neuter) "of bronze, brazen," modifying ἦτορ. **ἦτορ** (noun, nominative singular neuter) "heart" – subject in the clause. **ἐνείη** (verb, 3rd singular present optative active) "might be (in me)" from ἔνειμι, expressing an unreal condition. 

The poet continues his impossible wish: even if his voice were unbreakable and a bronze heart were within him, he still could not catalog all the ships without
491:
**Εἰ μὴ Ὀλυμπιάδες Μοῦσαι Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο**

**Ὀλυμπιάδες** (nom. pl. fem. adj.): "Olympian," modifying Μοῦσαι. **Μοῦσαι** (nom. pl. fem.): "Muses," subject of the implied verb (from next line). **Διὸς** (gen. sg. masc.): "of Zeus," possessive genitive. **αἰγιόχοιο** (gen. sg. masc. epithet): "aegis-bearing," modifying Διός. The poet invokes the Olympian Muses, daughters of aegis-bearing Zeus, acknowledging that without divine aid he cannot catalog all who came to Troy.
492: **θυγατέρες** (nom. pl. fem., "daughters") μνησαίαθʼ = **μνησαίατο** (aor. opt. mid., 3rd pl., "should recount, remember") **ὅσοι** (nom. pl. masc., "all who, as many as") **ὑπὸ** (prep. + acc., "to, toward") **Ἴλιον** (acc. sg., "Ilios, Troy") **ἦλθον** (aor. ind. act., 3rd pl., "came"). The poet appeals to the Olympian Muses, daughters of Zeus, to recount all who came to Troy, introducing the Catalogue of Ships.
493: **ἀρχούς** (acc. pl. masc., "leaders") and **νηῶν** (gen. pl. fem., "of the ships") establish the subject matter. **ἐρέω** (1st sg. fut. act. indic. of *εἶπον*/λέγω, "I shall tell") announces the catalogue's scope. **προπάσας** (acc. pl. fem., "all," intensive form of πᾶς) modifies νῆας (acc. pl., "ships"), emphasizing comprehensive enumeration. This programmatic verse introduces the Catalogue of Ships, promising to list both the commanders and their complete naval forces.
494:
**Βοιωτῶν μὲν Πηνέλεως καὶ Λήϊτος ἦρχον**

Βοιωτῶν (gen. pl., Βοιωτοί) "of the Boeotians"; μέν (particle) marks the first item in the Catalogue; Πηνέλεως and Λήϊτος (nom. sg., proper names) "Peneleos and Leitus," subjects; ἦρχον (3rd pl. impf. act. indic., ἄρχω) "were leading/commanded." The verse introduces the Boeotian contingent, the first in the Catalogue of Ships, with two of their five leaders named.
495:
**Ἀρκεσίλαός τε Προθοήνωρ τε Κλονίος τε** (Iliad 2.495)

**Ἀρκεσίλαός** (nom. sg. masc., proper name) "Arcesilaus"; **Προθοήνωρ** (nom. sg. masc., proper name) "Prothoenor"; **Κλονίος** (nom. sg. masc., proper name) "Clonius"; **τε... τε... τε** (enclitic conj.) "both... and... and," creating a tricolon. This line completes the list of five Boeotian commanders begun in the previous verse, naming the remaining three leaders with polysyndetic coordination.
496: **οἵ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who"; **ἐνέμοντο** (νέμω, 3rd pl. impf. mid.) "inhabited, dwelt in"; **Ὑρίην** (acc. sg. fem.) "Hyria" (place name); **Αὐλίδα** (acc. sg. fem.) "Aulis" (place name); **πετρήεσσαν** (adj. acc. sg. fem.) "rocky." The relative clause identifies warriors who inhabited Hyria and rocky Aulis, continuing the Boeotian catalogue.
497:
**Σχοῖνόν τε Σκῶλόν τε πολύκνημόν τʼ Ἐτεωνόν**

Σχοῖνόν (acc. sing., place name): Schoinos, a Boeotian town; Σκῶλόν (acc. sing., place name): Skolos, another Boeotian settlement; πολύκνημόν (acc. sing. masc./fem., compound adjective): "rich in ridges/slopes," epithet modifying Ἐτεωνόν; Ἐτεωνόν (acc. sing., place name): Eteonos, a Boeotian town. The line continues the catalog's enumeration of Boeotian settlements, with the poetic epithet emphasizing Eteonos' hilly terrain.
498: **Θέσπειαν** (acc. sing. fem., Thespeia, Boeotian city), **Γραῖάν** (acc. sing. fem., Graia, another Boeotian city), **εὐρύχορον** (acc. sing. fem. adj., "wide-dancing" or "with broad dancing-ground," compound of εὐρύς "wide" + χορός "dancing-place"), **Μυκαλησσόν** (acc. sing. fem., Mycalessus, Boeotian city). This line continues the Boeotian catalogue, listing four more cities in asyndetic sequence, with the ornamental epithet *eurychoron* distinguishing Mycalessus.
499:
**οἵ τʼ ἀμφʼ Ἅρμʼ ἐνέμοντο καὶ Εἰλέσιον καὶ Ἐρυθράς**

**οἵ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who, those who"; **ἀμφί** (preposition + acc., here elided before Ἅρμα) "around, about"; **ἐνέμοντο** (3rd pl. impf. mid. νέμω) "inhabited, occupied, held"; **Ἅρμα**, **Εἰλέσιον**, **Ἐρυθράς** (place names, acc.) "Harma," "Eilesion," and "Erythrae." The line continues the Catalogue of Ships, listing Boeot
500: **οἵ τʼ** (nom. pl. masc. relative pronoun with τε) "those who" continues the catalog listing. **Ἐλεῶνʼ** (acc. sg., Eleon) a Boeotian town. **εἶχον** (3rd pl. impf. act. indic. of ἔχω) "held, occupied." **Ὕλην** (acc. sg., Hyle) another Boeotian settlement. **Πετεῶνα** (acc. sg., Peteon) a third Boeotian town. The line enumerates three more Boeotian settlements controlled by the contingent, with the verb εἶχον governing all three accusative place names.
501:
**Ὠκαλέην Μεδεῶνά τʼ ἐϋκτίμενον πτολίεθρον**

Key words: **Ὠκαλέην** (acc. fem. sing., proper noun) "Ocalea"; **Μεδεῶνα** (acc. masc. sing., proper noun) "Medeon"; **ἐϋκτίμενον** (acc. neut. sing., perfect passive participle of εὖ + κτίζω) "well-built, well-founded"; **πτολίεθρον** (acc. neut. sing., noun) "citadel, town." 

This line continues the Boeotian catalog, listing Ocalea and the well-built citadel of Medeon as territories under Boeotian control.
502: **Κώπας** (acc. pl. fem.) – Copae, a Boeotian town; **Εὔτρησίν** (acc. sg. fem.) – Eutresis, another Boeotian town; **τε** (conj.) – "and," connecting items in the catalog; **πολυτρήρωνα** (acc. sg. fem.) – "rich in doves" or "with many doves," epithet modifying Thisbe; **Θίσβην** (acc. sg. fem.) – Thisbe, a Boeotian town. This line continues the Boeotian contingent in the Catalog of Ships, listing three towns with an ornamental epithet for the last.
503: **οἵ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "those who"; **τε** (enclitic particle) "and," connecting this clause with the preceding; **Κορώνειαν** (proper noun, acc. sing. fem.) "Coroneia," a Boeotian city; **ποιήενθʼ** (adjective, acc. sing. fem., < ποιήεις) "grassy" (with elided final -α); **Ἁλίαρτον** (proper noun, acc. sing. masc.) "Haliartus," another Boeotian city. The line continues the catalogue listing contingents, describing those who held Coroneia and grassy Haliartus.
504:
**οἵ τε Πλάταιαν ἔχον ἠδʼ οἳ Γλισᾶντʼ ἐνέμοντο**

Key words: **οἵ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc., "who/those who"), **Πλάταιαν** (proper noun, acc. sg. fem., "Plataea"), **ἔχον** (imperfect 3rd pl. of ἔχω, "they held/occupied"), **Γλισᾶντʼ** (proper noun, acc. sg. fem., "Glisas," with elided final alpha), **ἐνέμοντο** (imperfect 3rd pl. middle of νέμω, "they inhabited/dwelt in"). This verse continues the Boeotian catalogue, listing those who held
505: **Ὑποθήβας** (acc. pl., "Hypothebae"): city in Boeotia, often called "Lower Thebes." **εἶχον** (3rd pl. impf. act. indic. of ἔχω, "they held/occupied"): governing verb. **ἐϋκτίμενον** (acc. sg. masc./neut. perf. pass. part. of ἐυκτίζω, "well-built"): epithet modifying **πτολίεθρον** (acc. sg. neut., "citadel/town"). The line identifies those Boeotians who held the well-founded town of Hypothebae.
506:
**Ὀγχηστόν** (acc. sing., proper noun): Onchestus, a Boeotian town sacred to Poseidon. **ἱερόν** (acc. sing. neut. adj.): sacred, holy. **Ποσιδήϊον** (gen. sing., "of Poseidon"): possessive form indicating the grove belongs to Poseidon. **ἀγλαόν** (acc. sing. neut. adj.): splendid, glorious. **ἄλσος** (acc. sing. neut. noun): grove, sacred precinct. 

This line describes those who held Onchestus, specifically its sacred and splendid grove belonging to Poseidon, continuing the Boeotian catalogue.
507:
**Key words:** πολυστάφυλον (adj. acc. fem. sg. from πολυστάφυλος, "rich in grapes"), Ἄρνην (acc. fem. sg., Arne, a Boeotian city), ἔχον (3rd pl. impf. act. indic. from ἔχω, "held, possessed"), Μίδειαν (acc. fem. sg., Mideia, another Boeotian city).

The relative clause continues the catalogue, describing those who held grape-rich Arne and those who held Mideia; the epithet πολυστάφυλον emphasizes Boeotia's agricultural fertility.
508:
**Νῖσάν** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Nisa, a Boeotian city. **ζαθέην** (acc. sg. fem., adj.): "very holy, sacred," modifying Νῖσάν. **Ἀνθηδόνα** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Anthedon, another Boeotian city. **τʼ ἐσχατόωσαν** (acc. sg. fem., pres. part.): "situated on the coast/frontier," from ἐσχατόω, modifying Ἀνθηδόνα. 

This line continues the Boeotian catalogue, listing those who held sacred Nisa and coastal Anthedon, with formulaic epic epithets distinguishing each city.
509: **τῶν** (article, genitive plural masculine) "of these" — refers to the Boeotians mentioned in context. **πεντήκοντα** (numeral) "fifty" — the number of ships. **νέες** (noun, nominative plural feminine from ναῦς) "ships" — subject of the verb. **κίον** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect/aorist of εἶμι) "went, came" — describes the ships' movement. **ἑκάστῃ** (adjective, dative singular feminine) "in/on each" — refers to each individual ship.
510:
**κοῦροι** (nom. pl. masc., κοῦρος): "young men, warriors"; **Βοιωτῶν** (gen. pl., Βοιωτοί): "of the Boeotians"; **ἑκατὸν καὶ εἴκοσι**: "one hundred and twenty"; **βαῖνον** (3rd pl. impf., βαίνω): "were going, embarked." 

Each of the fifty Boeotian ships carried 120 young warriors, emphasizing the large contingent contributed by this region to the Greek expedition.
511: **οἳ** (rel. pron., nom. pl. masc.) "who" introduces relative clause describing the previous contingent. **Ἀσπληδόνα** (acc. sg. fem.) "Aspledon," and **Ὀρχομενὸν Μινύειον** (acc. sg. masc. with ethnic adj.) "Minyan Orchomenus" are objects of **ναῖον** (impf. 3rd pl., ναίω) "they dwelt in/inhabited." **ἰδέ** (conj.) "and" connects the two geographic locations.
512: **τῶν** (genitive plural, demonstrative pronoun) "of them"; **ἦρχʼ** (3rd singular imperfect, ἄρχω) "led, commanded"; **Ἀσκάλαφος** (nominative singular, proper noun) "Ascalaphus"; **Ἰάλμενος** (nominative singular, proper noun) "Ialmenus"; **υἷες** (nominative plural, υἱός) "sons"; **Ἄρηος** (genitive singular, proper noun) "of Ares." Ascalaphus and Ialmenus, sons of Ares, commanded these troops (from Aspledon and Orchomenus).
513: **οὓς** (relative pronoun, masculine accusative plural) "whom" — refers back to Ascalaphus and Ialmenus. **τέκεν** (aorist, 3rd singular of τίκτω) "bore/gave birth to" — indicates Astyoche as their mother. **Ἀστυόχη** (proper noun, nominative) "Astyoche" — the maiden who bore the sons. **δόμῳ** (dative singular of δόμος) "in the house" — locative, indicating where she bore them. **Ἄκτορος Ἀζεΐδαο** (genitive proper nouns) "of Actor, son of Azeus" — patronymic identification of Actor.
514:
**παρθένος αἰδοίη ὑπερώϊον εἰσαναβᾶσα**

παρθένος (noun, nom. sg. fem.): "maiden, virgin" — refers to Astyoche before her union with Ares. αἰδοίη (adj., nom. sg. fem.): "modest, reverent, chaste" — characterizes her maiden status. ὑπερώϊον (noun, acc. sg. neut.): "upper chamber" — the room where the encounter occurred. εἰσαναβᾶσα (participle, aor. nom. sg. fem., from εἰσαναβαίνω): "having gone up into" — describes her ascending to the chamber where Ares secretly lay with her.
515: **Ἄρηϊ κρατερῷ·** *Ἄρηϊ* (dat. sing. masc.) "to Ares," dative of the war god; *κρατερῷ* (dat. sing. masc. adj.) "mighty, strong," modifying Ἄρηϊ. **ὃ δέ** (nom. sing. masc. pron.) "and he," referring to Ares. **παρελέξατο** (3rd sing. aor. mid. indic.) "lay beside, slept with," from παραλέγομαι. **λάθρῃ** (dat. sing. fem.) "secretly, in secret," adverbial dative. The line describes Ares secretly sleeping with someone (likely Aphrodite in context).
516:
**τοῖς** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural masculine): "for these/them," referring to the Phocians mentioned in the next line.

**τριήκοντα** (numeral): "thirty," the number of ships.

**γλαφυραί** (adjective, nominative plural feminine): "hollow, curved," standard epithet for ships.

**νέες** (noun, nominative plural feminine): "ships," subject of the verb.

**ἐστιχόωντο** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect middle): "were marshaled/drawn up in rows," describing the arrangement of the Phocian contingent's thirty hollow ships.
517:
**αὐτὰρ** (δέ): "but, and" (postpositive conjunction, marking transition to new contingent). **Φωκήων** (Φωκεύς): genitive plural, "of the Phocians" (ethnic name). **Σχεδίος** and **Ἐπίστροφος**: nominative singular proper names, the two leaders. **ἦρχον** (ἄρχω): 3rd person dual imperfect active, "were leading, commanded."

The verse introduces the Phocian contingent with its dual commanders Schedius and Epistrophus, continuing the Catalogue's systematic enumeration of Greek forces.
518:
**υἷες Ἰφίτου μεγαθύμου Ναυβολίδαο,**

υἷες (nom. pl. masc., "sons") identifies Schedius and Epistrophus as the sons of Iphitus; Ἰφίτου (gen. sg. masc., "of Iphitus") is the father's name; μεγαθύμου (gen. sg. masc., "great-hearted," "noble-spirited") is an epithet modifying Iphitus; Ναυβολίδαο (gen. sg. masc., "son of Naubolus") is a patronymic identifying Iphitus as the son of Naubolus.
519:
**οἳ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who" — refers back to the sons of Iphitus. **Κυπάρισσον** (noun, acc. sg. fem.) "Cyparissus" — a town in Phocis. **ἔχον** (verb, 3rd pl. impf. act.) "held, occupied" — main verb. **Πυθῶνά** (noun, acc. sg. fem.) "Python" — alternative name for Delphi/Pytho. **πετρήεσσαν** (adj., acc. sg. fem.) "rocky" — describes Python/Pytho's mountainous terrain.

The line catalogues Phocian towns controlled by these leaders, emphasizing the sacred rocky site of Pytho/Delphi.
520: **Κρῖσάν** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Crisa, a town in Phocis near Delphi. **ζαθέην** (acc. sg. fem., adj.): "very holy, sacred," modifying Crisa. **Δαυλίδα** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Daulis, another Phocian town. **Πανοπῆα** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Panopeus, a third town in the Phocian catalog. This verse continues the list of Phocian contingents, emphasizing sacred Crisa (associated with Apollo's cult) alongside Daulis and Panopeus, all governed by the verb ἔχον from the broader catalog structure.
521: Key words: **οἵ** (relative pronoun, nominative plural masculine, "who/those who"), **Ἀνεμώρειαν** (proper noun, accusative singular feminine, "Anemorea," a Phocian town), **Ὑάμπολιν** (proper noun, accusative singular feminine, "Hyampolis," a Phocian town), **ἀμφενέμοντο** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect middle, "dwelt around" or "inhabited"). The line continues the catalogue of Phocian contingents, listing those who inhabited the areas around Anemorea and Hyampolis.
522:
**Key words:** πὰρ (preposition + acc.) "beside"; ποταμὸν (acc. sg. m. of ποταμός) "river"; Κηφισὸν (acc. sg. of Κηφισός) "Cephisus"; δῖον (acc. sg. m. of δῖος) "divine, goodly"; ἔναιον (3rd pl. impf. of ναίω) "they dwelt."

This line continues the Phocian catalogue, describing those who dwelt beside the divine river Cephisus, a major waterway in Phocis and Boeotia.
523:
**οἵ τε Λίλαιαν ἔχον πηγῇς ἔπι Κηφισοῖο·**

*οἵ* (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who"; *Λίλαιαν* (proper noun, acc. sg. fem.) "Lilaea," a Phocian town; *ἔχον* (imperfect, 3rd pl. of ἔχω) "held, occupied"; *πηγῇς* (noun, gen. sg. fem.) "of the source, spring"; *Κηφισοῖο* (proper noun, gen. sg. masc.) "of Cephisus" (river). Those who held Lilaea at the source of the Cephisus river.
524: **τοῖς** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural masculine): "with them," referring to the Phocian contingent. **τεσσαράκοντα** (numeral): "forty," the number of ships. **μέλαιναι** (adjective, nominative plural feminine): "black," modifying νῆες; conventional epithet for ships. **νῆες** (noun, nominative plural): "ships." **ἕποντο** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect middle): "were following" or "accompanied." This verse enumerates the Phocian naval contribution to the Greek expedition.
525: **οἳ** (demonstrative pronoun, nominative plural masculine) "these men" refers to the contingent just mentioned. **Φωκήων** (proper noun, genitive plural) "of the Phocians" indicates the troops being supported. **στίχας** (noun, accusative plural) "ranks, lines" denotes battle formations. **ἵστασαν** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect active) "were setting up, arranging." **ἀμφιέποντες** (participle, nominative plural masculine present active) "attending to, taking care of." These men were positioning and supporting the Phocian battle lines.
526: **Βοιωτῶν** (gen. pl. of Βοιωτοί) "of the Boeotians" – genitive of reference. **ἔμπλην** (adv.) "nearby, close at hand" – locative adverb. **ἀριστερά** (acc. pl. neut. of ἀριστερός) "on the left" – accusative of place where. **θωρήσσοντο** (3rd pl. imperf. mid./pass. of θωρήσσω) "were arming themselves" – describes the Boeotians taking their position and equipping themselves for battle on the left flank, near the Phocians mentioned in the previous line.
527: **Λοκρῶν** (gen. pl. of Λοκροί): "of the Locrians," genitive of the people governed by *ἡγεμόνευεν*. **ἡγεμόνευεν** (imperf. 3rd sg. of ἡγεμονεύω): "was leading, commanded," governing genitive. **Ὀϊλῆος** (gen. sg. of Ὀϊλεύς): "of Oileus," patronymic genitive. **ταχύς** (nom. sg. masc. of ταχύς): "swift," epithet of Ajax. **Αἴας** (nom. sg.): "Ajax," the lesser Ajax, son of Oileus, distinguished from Telamonian Ajax.
528: **μείων** (comparative adjective, nominative singular masculine) "smaller, lesser" – describes Ajax of Oileus; **τόσος** (demonstrative adjective, nominative singular masculine) "so great"; **ὅσος** (relative adjective, nominative singular masculine) "as great as" – together forming a correlative comparison "not so great as"; **Τελαμώνιος** (patronymic adjective, nominative singular masculine) "son of Telamon," referring to the greater Ajax. The line distinguishes the lesser Ajax of Oileus from his much larger namesake, Telamonian Ajax.
529:
**ἀλλὰ πολὺ μείων· ὀλίγος μὲν ἔην λινοθώρηξ,**

Key words: **μείων** (comparative adjective, nom. sg. masc., "smaller/lesser"), **ὀλίγος** (adjective, nom. sg. masc., "small"), **ἔην** (3rd sg. imperfect of εἰμί, "he was"), **λινοθώρηξ** (compound noun, nom. sg. masc., "wearing a linen corselet"). The line emphasizes Odysseus's physical smallness compared to Ajax, noting specifically that he wore a linen breastplate rather than bronze armor.
530:
**ἐγχείῃ** (dative singular, ἐγχείη) - "in spear-work"; **δʼ** (postpositive particle) - "but/and"; **ἐκέκαστο** (3rd singular pluperfect middle-passive, ἐκκαίνυμαι) - "he excelled, surpassed"; **Πανέλληνας** (accusative plural, Πανέλληνες) - "all the Hellenes"; **Ἀχαιούς** (accusative plural, Ἀχαιοί) - "Achaeans." 

The line states that this warrior excelled all the Hellenes and Achaeans in spear-work, emphasizing his martial superiority despite limited forces.
531:
**οἳ Κῦνόν τʼ ἐνέμοντʼ Ὀπόεντά τε Καλλίαρόν τε**

**οἵ** (nom. pl. masc., relative pronoun): "who"
**ἐνέμοντο** (3rd pl. imperf. mid., νέμω): "inhabited, occupied" (elided to ἐνέμοντ')
**Κῦνον, Ὀπόεντα, Καλλίαρον** (acc. sg., proper nouns): "Cynus, Opous, Calliaros" (cities in Locris)

This verse continues the Catalogue of Ships, listing cities controlled by the Locrians under Ajax son of Oileus.
532: **Βῆσσάν** (acc. sg., proper noun): Bessa, a town in Locris. **Σκάρφην** (acc. sg., proper noun): Scarphe, a Locrian city. **Αὐγειάς** (acc. pl., proper noun): Augeiae, Locrian settlements. **ἐρατεινάς** (acc. pl. fem. adj.): lovely, desirable. This verse continues the catalogue of Locrian cities, listing Bessa, Scarphe, and the lovely Augeiae among the territories of the Locrian contingent.
533:
**Τάρφην τε Θρόνιον τε Βοαγρίου ἀμφὶ ῥέεθρα·**

**Τάρφην** (acc. sing., fem.): "Tarphe," an accentually irregular accusative form of a Locrian place name. **Θρόνιον** (acc. sing., neut.): "Thronion," a town in the Locrian catalogue. **Βοαγρίου** (gen. sing., masc.): "of Boagrius," a river in Locris; genitive of specification with ῥέεθρα. **ἀμφί** (prep. + acc.): "around, near" the streams. **ῥέεθρα** (acc. pl., neut.): "streams, waters," from ῥέεθρον.
534:
**Key words:** τῷ (dat. sg. demonstrative pronoun, "with him"), τεσσαράκοντα (indeclinable numeral, "forty"), μέλαιναι (nom. pl. fem. adj., "black"), νῆες (nom. pl. fem. noun, "ships"), ἕποντο (3rd pl. imperf. mid./pass., "followed"). 

This line describes the forty black ships that accompanied Ajax the Lesser, leader of the Locrians mentioned in the next line.
535: **Λοκρῶν** (gen. pl., Lokroi) "of the Locrians"; **ναίουσι** (pres. act. indic. 3rd pl., naiō) "dwell, inhabit"; **πέρην** (adv./prep. + gen.) "across from, opposite"; **ἱερῆς** (gen. sg. fem., hieros) "holy, sacred"; **Εὐβοίης** (gen. sg., Euboia) "Euboea." This line identifies the Locrians who inhabit the territory opposite sacred Euboea, introducing the Opuntian Locrians under Ajax son of Oileus in the Catalogue of Ships.
536: **Εὔβοιαν** (acc. sg. fem., "Euboea") is the object of **ἔχον** (3rd pl. imperf. act., "held/occupied"). **μένεα πνείοντες** (acc. pl. neut. + nom. pl. masc. pres. act. part., "breathing might/fury") is a formulaic phrase characterizing the **Ἄβαντες** (nom. pl. masc., "Abantes"), the inhabitants of Euboea. This line introduces the Euboean contingent, famous for their martial spirit.
537:
**Χαλκίδα τʼ Εἰρέτριάν τε πολυστάφυλόν θʼ Ἱστίαιαν**

**Χαλκίδα** (acc. sg. fem.): Chalcis, major city on Euboea; **Εἰρέτριάν** (acc. sg. fem.): Eretria, another important Euboean city; **πολυστάφυλόν** (acc. sg. fem.): "rich in grapes," compound adjective (πολυ- + σταφυλή); **Ἱστίαιαν** (acc. sg. fem.): Histiaea, northern Euboean city. This verse continues the Euboean catalog, listing three cities held by the spirited Abantes, with Histiaea distinguished by its
538: **Κήρινθόν** (acc. sg. f., proper noun) "Cerinthos," object of ἔφαλον; **ἔφαλον** (3rd pl. impf. act., *ἐπέχω*) "they held/occupied"; **Δίου** (gen. sg. n., proper noun) "of Dion," dependent on πτολίεθρον; **αἰπὺ** (acc. sg. n., adj.) "steep, lofty"; **πτολίεθρον** (acc. sg. n., noun) "citadel, stronghold," object of ἔφαλον. The verse continues the catalog, listing those who held Cerinthos and the steep citadel of Dion.
539: **οἵ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who" – introduces a relative clause continuing the catalog of Euboean contingents. **Κάρυστον** (proper noun, acc. sg.) "Carystus" – a city on the southern coast of Euboea. **ἔχον** (imperfect, 3rd pl.) "held, occupied" – from ἔχω, denoting possession or control of territory. **Στύρα** (proper noun, acc. sg.) "Styra" – another Euboean town. **ναιετάασκον** (imperfect, 3rd pl.) "dwelt in, inhabited" – iterative/frequentative form of ναίω, emphasizing continuous habitation.
540: **τῶν** (pronoun, gen. pl. masc.) "of them" – genitive of the Abantes who held Carystus and Styra. **ἡγεμόνευʼ** (verb, 3rd sg. impf. act.) "was leader" – from ἡγεμονεύω, with elision before Ἐλεφήνωρ. **Ἐλεφήνωρ** (noun, nom. sg. masc.) "Elephenor" – the commander's name. **ὄζος** (noun, nom. sg. masc.) "scion, offshoot" – metaphorical designation meaning "descendant" or "branch." **Ἄρηος** (noun, gen. sg. masc.) "of Ares" – genitive of the war god's name, indicating heroic lineage or martial character.
541: **Χαλκωδοντιάδης** (patronymic nominative singular masculine): "son of Chalcodon," identifying Elephenor by his father's name. **μεγαθύμων** (adjective genitive plural masculine): "great-hearted," "high-spirited," modifying Ἀβάντων in the attributive position. **ἀρχὸς** (noun nominative singular masculine): "leader," "commander," functioning as predicate nominative with the understood subject Elephenor. **Ἀβάντων** (proper noun genitive plural): "of the Abantes," the Euboean tribe Elephenor commands. The line identifies Elephenor as the noble son of Chalcodon and leader of the great-hearted Abantes.
542: τῷ (demonstrative pronoun, dat. sg.) "with him"; ἅμα (adverb) "together with"; Ἄβαντες (noun, nom. pl.) "Abantes"; ἕποντο (verb, 3rd pl. impf. mid.) "followed"; θοοί (adj., nom. pl. masc.) "swift"; ὄπιθεν (adverb) "from behind, at the back"; κομόωντες (participle, nom. pl. masc. pres. act. of κομάω) "wearing long hair." The swift Abantes followed with him, wearing their hair long at the back.
543: **αἰχμηταί** (nom. pl. masc., "spearmen") **μεμαῶτες** (perf. part. nom. pl. masc. from μέμαα, "eager, striving") **ὀρεκτῇσι** (dat. pl. fem. from ὀρεκτός, "outstretched") **μελίῃσι** (dat. pl. fem., "ash-wood spears"). The line describes spearmen eager to pierce enemy breastplates with their outstretched ash-wood spears.
544: **θώρηκας** (acc. pl. m., θώραξ) "breastplates, corslets" — object of **�ρήξειν** (aor. act. inf., ῥήγνυμι) "to break, shatter," complementing the participle *μεμαῶτες* from the previous line. **δηΐων** (gen. pl. m., δήϊος) "of enemies, of foes" — possessive genitive. **ἀμφὴ στήθεσσι** (dat. pl. n., στῆθος with prep. ἀμφί) "around [their] chests." The spearmen are eager to shatter enemy breastplates around their chests with their outstretched ash-wood spears.
545:
**τῷ δʼ ἅμα τεσσαράκοντα μέλαιναι νῆες ἕποντο.**

*τῷ* (demonstrative pronoun, dat. sing. masc.) "with him"; *ἅμα* (adverb) "together, at the same time"; *τεσσαράκοντα* (numeral, indeclinable) "forty"; *μέλαιναι* (adjective, nom. pl. fem.) "black"; *νῆες* (noun, nom. pl.) "ships"; *ἕποντο* (verb, 3rd pl. impf. mid.) "followed, accompanied." This verse concludes a catalogue entry, stating that forty black ships followed with the leader.
546:
**Gloss for Iliad 2.546:**

*Ἀθήνας* (acc. pl., "Athens") is the direct object of *εἶχον* (3rd pl. imperf. act., "held/possessed"). *ἐϋκτίμενον* (acc. sg. neut. pple., "well-built") modifies *πτολίεθρον* (acc. sg., "citadel/city"). The line introduces the Athenian contingent, describing those who held Athens' well-founded citadel.
547: **δῆμον** (acc. sing. masc., "people/land") of **Ἐρεχθῆος** (gen. sing., "of Erechtheus") **μεγαλήτορος** (gen. sing. masc., "great-hearted," epithet modifying Erechtheus), **ὅν** (acc. sing. masc. relative pronoun, "whom") **ποτʼ** (enclitic adverb = ποτέ, "once"), **Ἀθήνη** (nom. sing., "Athena," subject of the following verb). The line identifies the Athenians as the people of great-hearted Erechtheus, whom Athena once reared (verb follows in next line).
548: **θρέψε** (aorist active indicative 3rd sg. of τρέφω): "nurtured, reared"; **Διὸς θυγάτηρ** (genitive + nominative): "daughter of Zeus" (i.e., Athena, subject of θρέψε); **τέκε** (aorist active indicative 3rd sg. of τίκτω): "bore, gave birth to"; **ζείδωρος ἄρουρα** (nominative feminine): "grain-giving earth," subject of τέκε. The line describes the miraculous birth of Erechtheus, whom the earth bore but Athena reared.
549:
**κὰδ δʼ ἐν Ἀθήνῃς εἷσεν ἑῷ ἐν πίονι νηῷ·**

*κὰδ* (= κατά + δέ): tmesis with preposition "down" or "in"; *Ἀθήνῃς*: locative form "in Athens"; *εἷσεν*: 3rd sg. aorist active indicative of ἵζω, "seated, established"; *πίονι*: adjective dat. sg. "rich, fertile"; *νηῷ*: dat. sg. "in the temple." "And down in Athens she established him in her own rich temple."
550: **ἔνθα** (adverb): "there," locating the worship at Athena's temple. **μιν** (pronoun, accusative singular): "him/her," referring to Erechtheus established in Athena's temple. **ταύροισι** (noun, dative plural from ταῦρος): "with bulls," instrumental dative of the sacrificial animals. **ἀρνειοῖς** (noun, dative plural from ἀρνειός): "with rams," paired with bulls as offerings. **ἱλάονται** (verb, 3rd plural present middle indicative from ἱλάομαι): "they propitiate/appease," describing the ritual worship.
551: **κοῦροι** (nom. pl. masc. of κοῦρος) "young men, youths"; **Ἀθηναίων** (gen. pl. of Ἀθηναῖος) "of the Athenians"; **περιτελλομένων** (gen. pl. pres. mid./pass. participle of περιτέλλομαι) "as they come round, revolving"; **ἐνιαυτῶν** (gen. pl. of ἐνιαυτός) "of years." The Athenian youths propitiate Erechtheus with sacrifices annually as the years cycle round.
552:
**Key words:** τῶν (genitive plural demonstrative pronoun, "of these/them"), ἡγεμόνευʼ (3rd sg. imperfect active indicative of ἡγεμονεύω, "was leader/commanded"), υἱὸς (nominative singular, "son"), Πετεῶο (genitive singular proper noun, "of Peteos"), Μενεσθεύς (nominative singular proper noun, "Menestheus"). 

The line states that Menestheus, son of Peteos, commanded these men (the Athenians mentioned in the previous line).
553: **τῷ** (dat. sing. masc. demonstrative pronoun) "to him/for him," referring to Menestheus. **ὁμοῖος** (nom. sing. masc. adj.) "equal, similar." **ἐπιχθόνιος** (nom. sing. masc. adj.) "upon the earth, earthly, mortal." **γένετο** (3rd sing. aor. mid. indic. of γίγνομαι) "was born, came to be." The line states that no other mortal man yet proved equal to Menestheus (in marshaling troops and horses).
554: **κοσμῆσαι** (aorist active infinitive of κοσμέω): "to marshal, arrange, order" (complementing the previous line's description of Nestor's unmatched ability). **ἵππους** (accusative plural masculine of ἵππος): "horses." **ἀνέρας** (accusative plural masculine of ἀνήρ): "men." **ἀσπιδιώτας** (accusative plural masculine of ἀσπιδιώτης): "shield-bearing men, warriors." This line completes the thought that no man was equal to Nestor in marshaling both cavalry and infantry forces; only Nestor could rival such skill, for he was of an earlier generation.
555: **Νέστωρ** (nom. sg. masc., proper name) "Nestor" – subject; **οἶος** (nom. sg. masc., adj.) "alone, only" – emphasizing Nestor's singular status; **ἔριζεν** (3rd sg. imperf. act., ἐρίζω) "contended, rivaled" – main verb; **προγενέστερος** (nom. sg. masc. comp., πρό + γίγνομαι) "elder-born, more ancient" – comparative adjective; **ἦεν** (3rd sg. imperf., εἰμί) "was" – copulative verb. Nestor alone rivaled Peleus in marshaling skill, for he was born earlier (i.e., of an older generation).
556:
**τῷ δʼ ἅμα πεντήκοντα μέλαιναι νῆες ἕποντο.**

*τῷ* (demonstrative pronoun, dative singular, "with him" = Nestor); *ἅμα* (adverb/preposition + dative, "together with"); *πεντήκοντα* (indeclinable numeral, "fifty"); *μέλαιναι* (adjective, nominative plural feminine, "black"); *ἕποντο* (imperfect middle/passive, 3rd plural of ἕπομαι, "were following"). Fifty black ships accompanied Nestor from Pylos.
557:
**Αἴας** (nom. sg. masc., proper name) "Ajax," subject of the sentence. **Σαλαμῖνος** (gen. sg. fem., Σαλαμίς) "from Salamis," indicating origin or point of departure. **ἄγεν** (3rd sg. impf. act. indic., ἄγω) "was leading/brought," main verb. **δυοκαίδεκα** (indecl. numeral) "twelve," modifying ships. **νῆας** (acc. pl. fem., ναῦς) "ships," direct object.

Ajax led twelve ships from Salamis in the catalogue of Greek forces.
558:
**στῆσε δʼ ἄγων ἵνʼ Ἀθηναίων ἵσταντο φάλαγγες.**

**στῆσε** (aorist active indicative, 3rd singular of ἵστημι): "he stationed" or "he drew up [his ships]." **ἄγων** (present active participle, nominative singular masculine of ἄγω): "leading" or "bringing." **ἵνʼ** (adverb, crasis for ἵνα): "where." **ἵσταντο** (imperfect middle indicative, 3rd plural of ἵστημι): "were standing" or "took their stand." **φάλαγγες** (nominative plural of φάλαγξ): "battle-lines" or "ranks." Ajax stationed his ships where the
559:
**οἳ** (pronoun, nom. pl. masc., relative): "who" or "those who," introducing a new contingent. **Ἄργός** (noun, acc. sg. neut.): "Argos," major city in the Peloponnese. **εἶχον** (verb, 3rd pl. imperf. act.): "held" or "occupied." **Τίρυνθά** (noun, acc. sg. fem.): "Tiryns," fortified city near Argos. **τειχιόεσσαν** (adj., acc. sg. fem.): "walled" or "well-fortified," epithet emphasizing Tiryns' massive Cyclopean walls. 

This line begins the Catalogue's entry for the Argive forces under Diomedes, listing the principal cities of the Argolid.
560:
**Ἑρμιόνην Ἀσίνην τε, βαθὺν κατὰ κόλπον ἐχούσας**

Key words: **Ἑρμιόνην** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Hermione, a city in the Argolid; **Ἀσίνην** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Asine, another Argolid city; **βαθὺν** (acc. sg. masc., adjective): deep; **κόλπον** (acc. sg. masc., noun): bay, gulf; **ἐχούσας** (acc. pl. fem., present participle of ἔχω): holding, occupying. The line continues the Catalogue's geographical description, listing two coastal cities characterized by their position on a deep bay.
561: **Τροιζῆνα** (acc. sg., "Troezen"), **Ἠϊόνας** (acc. pl., "Eiones"), **ἀμπελόεντα** (acc. sg., adj. from ἀμπελόεις, "rich in vines"), **Ἐπίδαυρον** (acc. sg., "Epidaurus"). This continues the Catalogue of Ships listing territories in the Argolid: Troezen, Eiones, and vine-rich Epidaurus, all accusative objects of "held" from the surrounding context.
562:
**Line:** οἵ τʼ ἔχον Αἴγιναν Μάσητά τε κοῦροι Ἀχαιῶν

**Gloss:** οἵ (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc., "who") introduces those holding Aegina and Mases. ἔχον (imperfect, 3rd pl., ἔχω, "held/occupied") indicates territorial control. Αἴγιναν and Μάσητά (accusatives, "Aegina" and "Mases") are the places held by these contingents. κοῦροι Ἀχαιῶν (nom. pl., "sons/youths of the Achaeans") is an epic formula designating the Greek warriors.
563: **τῶν** (demonstrative genitive plural, "of these") marks the transition to new leadership. **ἡγεμόνευε** (imperfect 3rd singular from ἡγεμονεύω, "was leading/commanding") describes military command. **βοὴν ἀγαθός** ("good at the war cry," nominative singular epithet) is a traditional formula for martial prowess. **Διομήδης** (nominative singular, "Diomedes") identifies the leader of these Argive contingents.
564:
**καὶ** (conjunction): "and," connecting Sthenelus to the previous leaders.

**Σθένελος** (proper noun, nominative singular): Sthenelus, son of Capaneus, one of the Greek leaders.

**Καπανῆος** (proper noun, genitive singular): "of Capaneus," patronymic identifying Sthenelus's father, one of the Seven against Thebes.

**ἀγακλειτοῦ** (adjective, genitive singular masculine): "very famous" or "most renowned," modifying Capaneus.

**φίλος υἱός** (adjective + noun, nominative singular): "dear son," in apposition to Sthenelus, emphasizing his filial relationship.
565:
**Key words:** τοῖσι (dat. pl. demonstrative pronoun, "with these"), ἅμα (adverb, "together with"), τρίτατος (nom. sg. masc. superlative adjective, "as third"), κίεν (3rd sg. imperfect of κίω, "went"), ἰσόθεος (nom. sg. masc. compound adjective, "godlike, equal to a god"), φώς (nom. sg. masc. noun, "man, hero"). 

With these two went Euryalus as third, a godlike man, emphasizing his status as the third leader of the Argive contingent.
566:
**Μηκιστέος υἱὸς Ταλαϊονίδαο ἄνακτος·**

Μηκιστέος (gen. sg. masc., "of Mecisteus") - patronymic genitive dependent on υἱός. υἱός (nom. sg. masc., "son") - subject identifying Euryalus. Ταλαϊονίδαο (gen. sg. masc., "son of Talaus") - patronymic genitive in apposition to Μηκιστέος, extending the genealogy. ἄνακτος (gen. sg. masc., "lord, prince") - genitive of apposition, emphasizing the noble status of Talaus.
567: **συμπάντων** (gen. pl. masc., πᾶς) "of all [them]" – genitive of the whole governed by ἡγεῖτο. **ἡγεῖτο** (3rd sg. imperf. mid., ἡγέομαι) "was leading, commanded" – takes genitive object. **βοὴν ἀγαθός** (nom. sg. masc., formulaic epithet) "good at the war-cry, mighty in battle" – standard epithet for warriors. **Διομήδης** (nom. sg., proper name) "Diomedes" – son of Tydeus, leader of the Argive contingent. The line establishes Diomedes as supreme commander of all the forces previously enumerated.
568: **τοῖσι** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural masculine): "for these," referring to Diomedes and his contingent. **ὀγδώκοντα** (numeral): "eighty." **μέλαιναι** (adjective, nominative plural feminine): "black," epithet for ships. **νῆες** (noun, nominative plural feminine): "ships." **ἕποντο** (verb, third person plural imperfect middle): "were following" or "accompanied." Eighty black ships accompanied Diomedes' forces from their cities.
569:
**οἳ δὲ Μυκήνας εἶχον ἐϋκτίμενον πτολίεθρον**

*οἳ* (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "those who"; *Μυκήνας* (proper noun, acc. pl.) "Mycenae"; *εἶχον* (imperfect act. ind., 3rd pl. of ἔχω) "held, possessed"; *ἐϋκτίμενον* (perfect passive participle, acc. sg. neut. of ἐϋκτίζω) "well-built, well-founded"; *πτολίεθρον* (noun, acc. sg. neut.) "citadel, city." This verse introduces the Mycenaean contingent led by Agamemnon in the Catalogue of Ships.
570:
**ἀφνειόν τε Κόρινθον ἐϋκτιμένας τε Κλεωνάς**

**ἀφνειόν** (adj., acc. sing. masc.): "wealthy, rich" modifying Κόρινθον. **Κόρινθον** (noun, acc. sing.): "Corinth," the wealthy city on the Isthmus. **ἐϋκτιμένας** (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. fem.): "well-built, well-founded" modifying Κλεωνάς. **Κλεωνάς** (noun, acc. pl. fem.): "Cleonae," a town in the Argolid. The verse catalogs cities held by the Achaeans, emphasizing Corinth's wealth and the well-built character of
571: **Ὀρνειάς** (acc. pl., proper noun) - "Orneiae," a city in the Argolid; **ἐνέμοντο** (3rd pl. impf. mid., νέμω) - "they inhabited" or "occupied"; **Ἀραιθυρέην** (acc. sg., proper noun) - "Araithyrea," another town; **ἐρατεινήν** (acc. sg. fem., ἐρατεινός) - "lovely" or "charming." The verse catalogues the cities controlled by these Achaean forces, with the middle voice of νέμω emphasizing their possession or habitation of these territories.
572: **Iliad 2.572**: Καὶ Σικυῶνα (accusative singular, "and Sicyon," city name); ὅθʼ = ὅθι (adverb, "where"); ἄρα (particle, "indeed/then"); Ἄδρηστος (nominative singular, "Adrastus," legendary king); πρῶτα (adverbial accusative, "first"); ἐμβασίλευεν (3rd singular imperfect, ἐμβασιλεύω, "ruled as king"). The verse catalogues Sicyon, where Adrastus first held royal power before his time at Argos.
573:
**οἵ θʼ Ὑπερησίην τε καὶ αἰπεινὴν Γονόεσσαν**

**οἵ** (rel. pron., nom. pl. masc.) "who" – continuing the catalogue of Achaean contingents; **Ὑπερησίην** (acc. sg. fem.) "Hyperesia" – place name, object of implied verb of holding/possessing; **αἰπεινὴν** (adj., acc. sg. fem.) "steep, lofty" – modifying **Γονόεσσαν**; **Γονόεσσαν** (acc. sg. fem.) "Gonoessa" – place name. The line lists territories held by the contingent, pairing two locations with asyndeton followed by copulative τε καὶ.
574:
**Πελλήνην** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun) "Pellene" (Achaean city); **εἶχον** (3rd pl. impf. act., ἔχω) "they held/possessed"; **Αἴγιον** (acc. sg. neut., proper noun) "Aigion" (Achaean coastal city); **ἀμφενέμοντο** (3rd pl. impf. mid., ἀμφινέμομαι) "they dwelt around/occupied." 

The line continues the Achaean catalogue, listing Pellene and Aigion as territories held and inhabited by these warriors.
575:
**Αἰγιαλόν** (acc. sg. m., "seacoast/shore") **τʼ** (enclitic conj., "and") **ἀνὰ** (prep. + acc., "throughout") **πάντα** (acc. sg. m., "all/entire") **καὶ** (conj., "and") **ἀμφʼ** (prep. + acc., "around/about") **Ἑλίκην** (acc. sg. f., "Helike," a city in Achaea) **εὐρεῖαν** (acc. sg. f., "broad/wide"). 

This line continues the catalog's description of Achaean territory, specifying "all the seacoast throughout and around broad Helike," using two prepositions (ἀνά, ἀμφί) to indicate geographical
576: **τῶν** (demonstrative pronoun, genitive plural masculine) "of these/them"; **ἑκατόν** (numeral) "hundred"; **νηῶν** (noun, genitive plural feminine from ναῦς) "of ships"; **ἦρχε** (verb, 3rd singular imperfect active from ἄρχω) "was commanding/ruled over"; **κρείων** (noun, nominative singular masculine) "lord/ruler"; **Ἀγαμέμνων** (proper noun, nominative) "Agamemnon." Lord Agamemnon commanded a hundred ships of these men, the genitive τῶν referring back to the Achaean contingent previously described.
577: **Ἀτρεΐδης** (nom. sg. patronymic) "son of Atreus," referring to Agamemnon; **ἅμα** (adv.) "together with"; **τῷ** (dat. sg. demonstrative pronoun) "him"; **πλεῖστοι** (nom. pl. masc. superlative adj.) "most numerous"; **ἄριστοι** (nom. pl. masc. superlative adj.) "best, bravest." The line emphasizes that with Agamemnon followed the most numerous and finest warriors.
578:
**λαοὶ** (nom. pl. masc., λαός): "peoples, troops" - subject of ἕποντο, the soldiers following Agamemnon. **ἕποντο** (3rd pl. imperf. mid., ἕπομαι): "were following" - describes the troops accompanying their leader. **ἐδύσετο** (3rd sg. aor. mid., δύω): "clothed himself in, put on" - Agamemnon arming himself. **νώροπα** (acc. sg. masc., νώροψ): "gleaming, bright" - epithet modifying χαλκόν. **χαλκόν** (acc. sg. masc., χαλκός): "bronze" - metonymy for bronze armor.

The troops were following, and he himself put on the gleaming bronze armor.
579: **κυδιόων** (pres. part. nom. sg. masc. of κυδιάω) "exulting, glorying"; **πᾶσιν** (dat. pl. masc. of πᾶς) "among all"; **μετέπρεπεν** (3rd sg. impf. of μεταπρέπω) "stood out, was conspicuous"; **ἡρώεσσιν** (dat. pl. of ἥρως) "heroes, warriors." Agamemnon stands out conspicuously among all the heroes while exulting in his armor.
580:
**οὕνεκʼ ἄριστος ἔην πολὺ δὲ πλείστους ἄγε λαούς.**

Key words: **οὕνεκα** (conjunction) "because"; **ἄριστος** (superlative adjective, nom. sg. masc.) "best, bravest"; **ἔην** (3rd sg. impf. of εἰμί) "he was"; **πλείστους** (superlative adjective, acc. pl. masc.) "most numerous"; **ἄγε** (3rd sg. impf. of ἄγω) "he led, brought"; **λαούς** (acc. pl. of λαός) "peoples, troops." This explains why the hero stood out among all the warriors: he was the best and brought by far the most men.
581:
**οἳ δʼ εἶχον κοίλην Λακεδαίμονα κητώεσσαν**

**οἳ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who, those who"; **εἶχον** (imperfect, 3rd pl. of ἔχω) "held, possessed"; **κοίλην** (adjective, acc. sg. fem.) "hollow, with valleys"; **Λακεδαίμονα** (proper noun, acc. sg.) "Lacedaemon" (Sparta); **κητώεσσαν** (adjective, acc. sg. fem.) "with ravines, full of clefts." This verse introduces the contingent from hollow, ravine-filled Lacedaemon (the region around Sparta).
582:
**Φᾶρίν τε Σπάρτην τε πολυτρήρωνά τε Μέσσην,**

Φᾶρίν (acc. sg. fem., "Pharae," a town in Lacedaemon) and Σπάρτην (acc. sg. fem., "Sparta," the principal city) are coordinated objects of εἶχον/ἐνέμοντο from the surrounding context. πολυτρήρωνα (acc. sg. fem., compound adj., "full of doves" or "rich in pigeons") modifies Μέσσην (acc. sg. fem., "Messē," a Laconian town). The line continues the catalogue's enumeration of Lacedaemonian territories under Menelaus's control.
583:
**Βρυσειάς τʼ ἐνέμοντο καὶ Αὐγειὰς ἐρατεινάς**

*ἐνέμοντο* (3rd pl. impf. mid. of νέμω): "they inhabited/occupied," continuing the catalogue of Laconian territories. *Βρυσειάς* (acc. pl. fem.): "Bryseiai," a town in Lacedaemon. *Αὐγειάς* (acc. pl. fem.): "Augeiai," another Laconian settlement. *ἐρατεινάς* (acc. pl. fem. adj.): "lovely/desirable," an epithet emphasizing the attractiveness of Augeiai.
584:
**Key words:** 
- **Ἀμύκλας** (acc. pl. f.): Amyclae, a town in Laconia near Sparta
- **εἶχον** (3rd pl. imperf. act.): "held, possessed" from ἔχω
- **Ἕλος** (acc. sg. n.): Helos, a coastal town in Laconia
- **ἔφαλον** (acc. sg. n. adj.): "maritime, coastal" modifying πτολίεθρον
- **πτολίεθρον** (acc. sg. n.): "citadel, town"

This continues the Laconian catalogue, listing those who held Amyclae and Helos, the coastal citadel.
585:
**Gloss for οἵ τε Λάαν εἶχον ἠδʼ Οἴτυλον ἀμφενέμοντο:**

**οἵ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who"; **εἶχον** (imperfect active, 3rd pl. ἔχω) "held, possessed"; **ἠδʼ** (conjunction = ἠδέ) "and"; **Οἴτυλον** (acc. sg. masc.) "Oitylos" (Laconian town); **ἀμφενέμοντο** (imperfect middle, 3rd pl. ἀμφινέμομαι) "dwelt around, inhabited." The line continues the Lacedaemonian catalogue, listing those who held Laas and dwelt around Oity
586: **τῶν** (demonstrative genitive plural) "of them"; **ἀδελφεὸς** (noun nominative singular) "brother," referring to Menelaus as Agamemnon's brother; **ἦρχε** (imperfect 3rd singular of ἄρχω) "was leading, commanded"; **βοὴν ἀγαθὸς** (formulaic epithet, accusative + adjective nominative) "good at the war-cry," standard heroic phrase modifying Menelaus. Menelaus, Agamemnon's brother distinguished by his battle-cry, commanded these contingents separately from the main Achaean forces.
587:
**ἑξήκοντα νεῶν· ἀπάτερθε δὲ θωρήσσοντο·**

**ἑξήκοντα** (numeral, indeclinable): "sixty," modifying νεῶν. **νεῶν** (noun, genitive plural of ναῦς): "of ships," genitive of number with the numeral. **ἀπάτερθε** (adverb): "apart, separately," indicating Menelaus' ships were positioned distinctly. **θωρήσσοντο** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect middle-passive of θωρήσσω): "they were arming themselves," the crews preparing for battle. Menelaus commanded sixty ships that were arrayed separately, the men arming themselves according to his own eager initiative.
588:
**Key words:** *κίεν* (3rd sg. impf. of κίω, "he went"); *ᾗσι* (dat. pl. fem. possessive adj., "his own"); *προθυμίῃσι* (dat. pl. of προθυμίη, "eagerness, zeal"); *πεποιθώς* (perf. act. ptc. of πείθω, "trusting in, confident"). 

Nestor himself went among them, trusting in his own eagerness/zeal for battle.
589: **ὀτρύνων** (pres. act. ptc. nom. sg. masc., ὀτρύνω) "urging on, rousing"; **πόλεμον** (acc. sg. masc., πόλεμος) "war, battle"; **μάλιστα** (adv. superl.) "most of all, especially"; **ἵετο** (imperf. mid. 3rd sg., ἵημι) "he rushed, hastened"; **θυμῷ** (dat. sg. masc., θυμός) "in spirit, with his heart." Agamemnon urges on the battle, and most of all his spirit hastens (to engage).
590: **τίσασθαι** (aorist middle infinitive of τίνω): "to avenge, exact requital for"; **Ἑλένης** (genitive singular of Ἑλένη): "of Helen," objective genitive with the infinitive; **ὁρμήματά** (accusative plural neuter of ὅρμημα): "onsets, attacks, assaults"; **στοναχάς** (accusative plural feminine of στοναχή): "groans, lamentations." The line expresses the desire to exact vengeance for Helen's attacks and groans, with both accusatives as objects of the infinitive τίσασθαι.
591:
**οἳ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who" – introduces a new contingent. **Πύλον** (proper noun, acc. sg.) "Pylos" – Nestor's principal city. **ἐνέμοντο** (verb, 3rd pl. imperf. mid. νέμω) "inhabited, occupied" – describes territorial possession. **Ἀρήνην** (proper noun, acc. sg.) "Arene" – a Messenian town. **ἐρατεινήν** (adjective, acc. sg. fem.) "lovely, desirable" – formulaic epithet for cities.

This verse begins the Pylian contingent, listing the territories under Nestor's command in southwest Messenia.
592:
**καὶ Θρύον Ἀλφειοῖο πόρον καὶ ἐΰκτιτον Αἰπύ**

**Θρύον** (acc. sing.): Thryoum, a town in Nestor's realm. **Ἀλφειοῖο** (gen. sing.): of the Alpheius, the major river of Elis and Messenia. **πόρον** (acc. sing.): ford, crossing-place. **ἐΰκτιτον** (acc. sing., fem.): well-built, well-founded (compound adjective from εὖ + κτίζω). **Αἰπύ** (acc. sing.): Aipy, another settlement in Nestor's territory. The line lists towns controlled by Nestor's contingent, including Thry
593:
**Gloss for: καὶ Κυπαρισσήεντα καὶ Ἀμφιγένειαν ἔναιον**

*Κυπαρισσήεντα* (acc. sg., "Cyparisseis," toponym with adjectival form meaning "rich in cypresses"), *Ἀμφιγένειαν* (acc. sg., "Amphigeneia," place name), and *ἔναιον* (3rd pl. impf. act. indic. of ναίω, "they dwelt/inhabited") are the key terms. This line continues the catalog of Pylian cities, listing two settlements inhabited by Nestor's people.
594: **Πτελεόν** (acc. sg. n.): Pteleon, a town in Thessaly. **Ἕλος** (acc. sg. n.): Helos, another Thessalian town. **Δώριον** (acc. sg. n.): Dorion, where the Muses encountered Thamyris. **ἔνθα** (adv.): where, at which place. **Μοῦσαι** (nom. pl. f.): the Muses, goddesses of song and poetry. The line catalogues three towns culminating in Dorion, introducing the locale of the Muses' fateful meeting with the Thracian bard Thamyris.
595: **ἀντόμεναι** (pres. part. nom. pl. fem., "meeting, encountering") **Θάμυριν** (acc. sg. masc., "Thamyris," Thracian bard) **Θρήϊκα** (acc. sg. masc., "Thracian") **παῦσαν** (aor. act. indic. 3rd pl., "they stopped, caused to cease") **ἀοιδῆς** (gen. sg. fem., "from song, of singing"). The Muses, encountering the Thracian singer Thamyris, stopped him from his singing—a reference to the mythic punishment for his hubristic challenge to the goddesses.
596:
**Οἰχαλίηθεν** (adverb, -θεν suffix): "from Oechalia," indicating motion/origin from the city. **ἰόντα** (present participle, accusative singular masculine of εἶμι): "going," modifying Thamyris. **παρʼ** (preposition + genitive): "from (the presence of)," indicating departure. **Εὐρύτου** (genitive singular): "of Eurytus," the king. **Οἰχαλιῆος** (genitive singular adjective): "Oechalian," epithet modifying Eurytus.

The line describes Thamyris traveling from Oechalia, having left the court of Eurytus the Oechalian.
597: **στεῦτο** (3rd sg. impf. mid. of στεύομαι) "he boasted"; **εὐχόμενος** (pres. mid. participle nom. sg. masc. of εὔχομαι) "boasting, vaunting"; **νικησέμεν** (fut. inf. of νικάω) "that he would defeat"; **εἴ περ ἂν** "even if" (conditional with potential force); **αὐταί** (nom. pl. fem. of αὐτός) "they themselves." The singer Thamyris boasted he would defeat even the Muses themselves in song.
598:
**Μοῦσαι** (nom. pl. fem., "Muses") **ἀείδοιεν** (3rd pl. pres. opt. act., "should sing") **κοῦραι** (nom. pl. fem., "daughters") **Διὸς** (gen. sg., "of Zeus") **αἰγιόχοιο** (gen. sg. masc., "aegis-bearing"). 

Thamyris boasted he would conquer even if the Muses themselves, daughters of aegis-bearing Zeus, should sing against him; the appositive *κοῦραι Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο* emphasizes their divine parentage and authority.
599:
**Key words:** χολωσάμεναι (aorist middle participle nominative feminine plural of χολόομαι, "becoming angry"); πηρὸν (adjective accusative masculine singular, "maimed, blind"); θέσαν (3rd plural aorist active indicative of τίθημι, "made"); ἀοιδὴν (noun accusative feminine singular, "song").

The Muses, angered, made Thamyris maimed/blind and took away his divine song, with the causal participle indicating their wrath as the motivation for this punishment.
600: **θεσπεσίην** (adj., fem. acc. sg., "divine, wondrous") modifies ἀοιδήν from the previous line; **ἀφέλοντο** (aor. mid. indic., 3rd pl. of ἀφαιρέω, "they took away"); **ἐκλέλαθον** (pluperfect act. indic., 3rd pl. of ἐκλανθάνω, "they made [him] forget"); **κιθαριστύν** (noun, fem. acc. sg., "lyre-playing, skill at the lyre"). The Muses, angered, took away Thamyris' divine song and made him forget his mastery of the lyre.
601: **τῶν** (gen. pl. demonstrative pronoun) "of them/their" — **αὖθʼ** (adverb, < αὖτε) "in turn, moreover" — **ἡγεμόνευε** (3rd sg. impf. act. indic., ἡγεμονεύω) "was leading, commanded" — **Γερήνιος** (nom. sg. masc. adj.) "Gerenian" (epithet) — **ἱππότα** (nom./acc. sg. masc., ἱππότης) "horseman, knight" — **Νέστωρ** (nom. sg. proper noun) "Nestor." Nestor, the Gerenian horseman, in turn commanded them (the Pylians and their ninety ships).
602:
**τῷ δʼ ἐνενήκοντα γλαφυραὶ νέες ἐστιχόωντο.**

*τῷ* (dat. sg. masc. demonstrative pronoun) "for him," referring to Nestor; *ἐνενήκοντα* (indeclinable numeral) "ninety"; *γλαφυραί* (nom. pl. fem. adj.) "hollow, curved" (epithet of ships); *νέες* (nom. pl. fem. noun) "ships"; *ἐστιχόωντο* (3rd pl. imperf. mid.-pass. *στιχάω*) "were drawn up in rows, were arrayed."
603:
**οἳ δʼ ἔχον Ἀρκαδίην ὑπὸ Κυλλήνης ὄρος αἰπὺ**

*οἳ* (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who" – introduces a new contingent; *ἔχον* (imperfect, 3rd pl. of ἔχω) "held, occupied"; *Ἀρκαδίην* (acc. sg. fem.) "Arcadia"; *ὑπὸ Κυλλήνης ὄρος αἰπὺ* "beneath steep Mount Cyllene" – *ὑπό* + acc. indicates location, *αἰπὺ* (nom./acc. sg. neut.) "steep, lofty" modifies *ὄρος
604:
**Αἰπύτιον παρὰ τύμβον ἵνʼ ἀνέρες ἀγχιμαχηταί,**

*Αἰπύτιον* (adj. acc. sg. masc.): "of Aepytus," modifying τύμβον; *παρά* (prep. + acc.): "beside"; *τύμβον* (noun acc. sg.): "tomb, burial mound"; *ἵνα* (adv.): "where"; *ἀγχιμαχηταί* (noun nom. pl. masc.): "close-fighters, hand-to-hand warriors." The line locates Arcadians near the tomb of Aepytus, where men are skilled in close combat.
605:
**Key words:** οἵ (nominative plural masculine relative pronoun, "who"), Φενεόν (accusative singular proper noun, Pheneos, a city in Arcadia), ἐνέμοντο (3rd plural imperfect middle indicative of νέμω, "inhabited/dwelt in"), Ὀρχομενόν (accusative singular proper noun, Orchomenos, an Arcadian city), πολύμηλον (accusative singular adjective, "rich in flocks/sheep," modifying Orchomenos).

The line catalogues Arcadian warriors who inhabited Pheneos and sheep-rich Orchomenos, continuing the geographical enumeration of Greek forces.
606:
**Ῥίπην τε Στρατίην τε καὶ ἠνεμόεσσαν Ἐνίσπην**

Ῥίπην (acc. sg. fem.): Rhipe, a town in Arcadia. Στρατίην (acc. sg. fem.): Stratie, another Arcadian town. ἠνεμόεσσαν (acc. sg. fem., adj.): "windy," from ἠνεμόεις, modifying Ἐνίσπην. Ἐνίσπην (acc. sg. fem.): Enispe, an Arcadian town. The line continues the catalogue of Arcadian territories, with all place names as direct objects of ἐνέμοντο/εἶχον from the surrounding context.
607:
**καὶ Τεγέην εἶχον καὶ Μαντινέην ἐρατεινὴν**

**Τεγέην** (acc. sing. fem., proper noun): Tegea, an Arcadian city. **εἶχον** (3rd pl. imperf. act. indic., ἔχω): "they held/possessed." **Μαντινέην** (acc. sing. fem., proper noun): Mantinea, another Arcadian city. **ἐρατεινὴν** (acc. sing. fem., adj., ἐρατεινός): "lovely, desirable." This line continues the Catalogue's enumeration of Arcadian territories, listing Tegea and lovely Mantinea as possessions of the contingent.
608:
**Στύμφηλόν τʼ εἶχον καὶ Παρρασίην ἐνέμοντο**

Στύμφηλόν (acc. sg.): Stymphelus, Arcadian city; τʼ (enclitic particle): and; εἶχον (3rd pl. impf. act. of ἔχω): they held/possessed; Παρρασίην (acc. sg.): Parrhasie, Arcadian region; ἐνέμοντο (3rd pl. impf. mid. of νέμω): they inhabited/dwelt in. The line continues the catalog of Arcadian territories, pairing two verbs of possession/habitation with their respective geographical objects.
609: **τῶν** (genitive plural demonstrative pronoun) "of them"; **ἦρχ(ε)** (3rd singular imperfect, ἄρχω) "was ruling/commanding"; **Ἀγκαίοιο** (genitive singular, Ἀγκαῖος) "of Ancaeus"; **πάϊς** (nominative singular) "son"; **κρείων** (nominative singular, present participle of κραίνω, or epithet) "lord/ruler"; **Ἀγαπήνωρ** (nominative singular, Ἀγαπήνωρ) "Agapenor." Of these (Arcadians), the son of Ancaeus, lord Agapenor, was commander.
610: **ἑξήκοντα** (numeral, nominative/accusative): "sixty" - modifying νεῶν in a partitive construction. **νεῶν** (noun, genitive plural of ναῦς): "of ships" - partitive genitive with the numeral. **πολέες** (adjective, nominative plural of πολύς): "many (men)" - subject of the implied verb, describing the Arcadians. **νηῒ** (noun, dative singular of ναῦς): "in (each) ship" - locative dative. **ἑκάστῃ** (adjective, dative singular of ἕκαστος): "each" - modifying νηΐ to indicate distribution across the ships.
611: **Ἀρκάδες** (nom. pl. masc., Ἀρκάς): "Arcadians," inhabitants of Arcadia in the central Peloponnese. **ἄνδρες** (nom. pl. masc., ἀνήρ): "men," warriors. **ἔβαινον** (3rd pl. impf. act. indic., βαίνω): "embarked," "went aboard." **ἐπιστάμενοι** (nom. pl. masc. pres. mid. participle, ἐπίσταμαι): "knowing how," "skilled in." **πολεμίζειν** (pres. act. infin., πολεμίζω): "to make war," "to fight." The Arcadian warriors, experienced in warfare, boarded the ships (sixty mentioned in the previous line).
612: **αὐτὸς** (pronoun, nominative singular masculine): "himself" - emphasizes that Agamemnon personally provided the ships. **δῶκεν** (verb, 3rd singular aorist active indicative of δίδωμι): "gave, provided." **ἄναξ** (noun, nominative singular): "lord, king" - in apposition to the subject. **Ἀγαμέμνων** (proper noun, nominative singular): Agamemnon, commander of the Greek forces, who supplied ships to the Arcadians (a land-locked people) so they could sail across the wine-dark sea.
613: νῆας (noun, acc. pl. f. from ναῦς): "ships" - direct object of περάαν. ἐϋσσέλμους (adj, acc. pl. f. from ἐΰσσελμος): "well-benched" - compound epithet modifying νῆας. περάαν (inf. aor. act. from περάω/περόω): "to cross, convey across" - epexegetic infinitive explaining the gift. οἴνοπα (adj, acc. sg. m. from οἰνοψ): "wine-dark" - formulaic epithet modifying πόντον. The line describes Agamemnon's gift of ships to cross the wine-dark sea.
614: **Ἀτρεΐδης** (nom. sg. masc., patronymic) "son of Atreus" (i.e., Agamemnon); **οὔ** (adv.) "not"; **σφι** (dat. pl. pron.) "to them"; **θαλάσσια ἔργα** (nom. pl. neut.) "sea matters, naval affairs"; **μεμήλει** (3rd sg. perf. act. indic. of μέλω) "was a care, was of concern." The son of Atreus provided ships because seafaring was not their concern.
615:
**Key words:** οἳ (nom. pl. masc. relative pronoun, "who/those who"), ἄρα (particle, "then/indeed"), Βουπράσιόν (acc. sg., toponym "Bouprasion"), Ἤλιδα (acc. sg., toponym "Elis"), δῖαν (acc. sg. fem., "divine/goodly"), ἔναιον (3rd pl. impf. act., "dwelt/inhabited"). 

The line introduces those who inhabited Bouprasion and divine Elis, with the accusatives governed by the verb ἔναιον.
616: **ὅσσον** (relative pronoun, neuter accusative singular of ὅσος) "as much as" or "all that which" introduces the extent of territory. **ἐφ'** (preposition ἐπί + smooth breathing from following vowel) "over" or "upon" governs the following place names. **Ὑρμίνη** (proper noun, feminine nominative/accusative) Hyrmina, a city in Elis. **Μύρσινος** (proper noun, feminine nominative) Myrsinus, another Elian city. **ἐσχατόωσα** (adjective, feminine nominative singular, present participle form of ἔσχατος) "being on the border" or "outermost," modifying Myrsinus.
617:
**πέτρη** (nom. sg. fem., "rock") **τʼ Ὠλενίη** (nom. sg. fem. adj., "Olenian") **καὶ Ἀλήσιον** (acc. sg. neut., place name "Alesion") **ἐντὸς** (adv., "within, inside") **ἐέργει** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of εἴργω, "encloses, contains"). 

This line continues the geographical description, listing the Olenian rock and Alesion as boundaries that enclose the territory within.
618:
**τῶν** (pronoun, genitive plural, demonstrative) "of these/them"; **τέσσαρες** (adjective, nominative plural) "four"; **ἀρχοί** (noun, nominative plural) "leaders, commanders"; **ἔσαν** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect of εἰμί) "were"; **δέκα** (numeral) "ten"; **ἑκάστῳ** (adjective, dative singular) "to each one." 

Of these men there were four leaders, and ten ships followed each one.
619: **νῆες** (nom. pl. f., "ships") **ἕποντο** (3rd pl. imperf. mid., "followed, accompanied"), **θοαί** (nom. pl. f. adj., "swift"), **πολέες** (nom. pl. m., "many"), **ἔμβαινον** (3rd pl. imperf., "embarked, went aboard"), **Ἐπειοί** (nom. pl. m., "Epeians"). The swift ships followed [each leader], and many Epeians embarked on them, continuing the catalog's enumeration of contingents and their commanders.
620:
**τῶν μὲν ἄρʼ Ἀμφίμαχος καὶ Θάλπιος ἡγησάσθην**

τῶν (gen. pl. demonstrative pronoun) "of these/them"; Ἀμφίμαχος and Θάλπιος (nom. sg. proper nouns) "Amphimachus and Thalpius," the two leaders; ἡγησάσθην (3rd dual aor. mid. indic. of ἡγέομαι) "led" or "were leaders." The dual verb form indicates these two heroes jointly commanded the Epeian contingent.
621: **υἷες** (nom. pl. m., "sons") identifies the subject as the sons of Cteatus and Eurytus. **Κτεάτου** and **Εὐρύτου** (gen. sg., "of Cteatus," "of Eurytus") are patronymics showing parentage, with **ὃ μέν... ὃ δέ** ("the one... the other") distinguishing Amphimachus from Thalpius. **Ἀκτορίωνε** (nom. dual, "descendants of Actor") is a dual patronymic indicating their lineage through Actor, grandfather of the twin brothers.
622:
**τῶν δʼ Ἀμαρυγκεΐδης ἦρχε κρατερὸς Διώρης·**

**Ἀμαρυγκεΐδης** (nom. sg. masc., patronymic): "son of Amarynceus"; **ἦρχε** (3rd sg. imperf. act., ἄρχω): "led, commanded"; **κρατερὸς** (nom. sg. masc., adj.): "mighty, strong"; **Διώρης** (nom. sg. masc., proper name): "Diores." The son of Amarynceus, mighty Diores, commanded them (the third contingent).
623:
**τῶν δὲ τετάρτων ἦρχε Πολύξεινος θεοειδὴς**

*τῶν* (demonstrative genitive plural): "of these/them," indicating the troops being described; *τετάρτων* (ordinal adjective genitive plural): "fourth," marking the fourth contingent in the catalogue; *ἦρχε* (imperfect 3rd singular of ἄρχω): "was leading/commanded"; *Πολύξεινος* (proper name nominative): Polyxeinus, the leader's name; *θεοειδὴς* (adjective nominative singular): "godlike," the standard Homeric epithet meaning "god-resembling" or "divine in appearance."
624:
**υἱὸς** (noun, nom. sg. masc.) "son" — identifies Polyxeinos's parentage. **Ἀγασθένεος** (proper noun, gen. sg. masc.) "of Agasthenes" — patronymic genitive. **Αὐγηϊάδαο** (proper noun, gen. sg. masc.) "of Augeias" — grandfather's name in the genitive, forming a longer genealogy. **ἄνακτος** (noun, gen. sg. masc.) "of the lord/prince" — in apposition to Augeias, indicating his royal status.

The line completes Polyxeinos's genealogy: he is the son of Agasthenes, himself son of the royal Augeias.
625:
**οἳ δʼ ἐκ Δουλιχίοιο Ἐχινάων θʼ ἱεράων**

*οἳ* (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.): "those who"; *Δουλιχίοιο* (proper noun, gen. sg.): "of Dulichium," genitive of place from which; *Ἐχινάων* (proper noun, gen. pl.): "of the Echinades," paired with Dulichium; *ἱεράων* (adjective, gen. pl. fem.): "sacred," modifying the islands (νήσων understood). This line introduces warriors from Dulichium and the sacred Echinades islands.
626:
**νήσων, αἳ ναίουσι πέρην ἁλὸς Ἤλιδος ἄντα,**

**νήσων** (gen. pl. of νῆσος): "of the islands," genitive dependent on the previous line's place names. **ναίουσι** (3rd pl. pres. act. indic. of ναίω): "they dwell/are situated." **πέρην** (adv./prep. + gen.): "beyond, on the far side of." **ἁλός** (gen. sg. of ἅλς): "the sea." **Ἤλιδος ἄντα** (gen. + prep.): "opposite Elis," indicating location across from the mainland territory.
627:
**Key words:** τῶν (genitive plural demonstrative pronoun) "of these/them," referring to the previously mentioned islanders; ἡγεμόνευε (3rd singular imperfect active indicative of ἡγεμονεύω) "was leading/commanding"; Μέγης (nominative singular proper noun) "Meges," the leader's name; ἀτάλαντος (nominative singular adjective) "equal to, like"; Ἄρηϊ (dative singular proper noun) "to Ares," the war god.

Meges, equal to Ares in martial prowess, commanded these island contingents; the verse establishes his leadership and martial excellence through the epic formula comparing him to the god of war.
628: **Φυλεΐδης** (patronymic nominative singular): "son of Phyleus," identifying Meges by his father's name. **τίκτε** (aorist indicative 3rd singular from τίκτω): "bore, gave birth to," describing his mother's act. **Διῒ φίλος** (dative + adjective): "dear to Zeus," a common epithet marking divine favor. **ἱππότα** (nominative singular): "horseman," an epithet for Phyleus. **Φυλεύς** (nominative singular): Meges' father, who appears as subject of the relative clause introduced by **ὅν**.
629: **ὅς** (relative pronoun, nom. sg. masc.) "who" refers back to Meges. **ἀπενάσσατο** (aorist middle, 3rd sg. of ἀπο-νάσσομαι) "departed to," "emigrated to." **Δουλίχιον** (acc. sg. neut.) the island of Doulichion, destination of migration. **πατρί** (dat. sg. masc.) "with his father," dative of accompaniment or association. **χολωθείς** (aorist passive participle, nom. sg. masc. of χολόομαι) "having become angry," "in anger." Meges emigrated to Doulichion after a quarrel with his father Phyleus.
630: τῷ (pronoun, dative singular masculine demonstrative) "with him" refers to the leader just mentioned. τεσσαράκοντα (numeral) "forty" specifies the fleet size. μέλαιναι (adjective, nominative plural feminine) "black" describes the ships, a common Homeric epithet. νῆες (noun, nominative plural) "ships" is the subject. ἕποντο (verb, 3rd plural imperfect middle) "were following" indicates the ships accompanied him to Troy.
631: **αὐτὰρ** (particle): "but, and" – marks transition to a new contingent in the Catalogue of Ships. **Ὀδυσσεὺς** (nom. sg. masc.): "Odysseus" – subject, the hero leads his people. **ἦγε** (3rd sg. impf. act., ἄγω): "was leading, led" – main verb governing the contingent. **Κεφαλλῆνας** (acc. pl. masc.): "Cephallenians" – object, the people under Odysseus's command from his island realm. **μεγαθύμους** (acc. pl. masc., adj.): "great-hearted, high-spirited" – standard epithet for heroic warriors.
632: **Key words:** οἵ (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc., "who"), εἶχον (imperfect active 3rd pl. of ἔχω, "held/possessed"), Ἰθάκην (acc. sg. fem., "Ithaca"), Νήριτον (acc. sg. masc., "Neritum," a mountain), εἰνοσίφυλλον (acc. sg. masc. adj., "leaf-shaking" or "with trembling leaves"). The line catalogues the territories held by Odysseus's contingent, specifying Ithaca and leafy Neritum.
633:
**καὶ Κροκύλειʼ ἐνέμοντο καὶ Αἰγίλιπα τρηχεῖαν**

*Κροκύλειʼ* (Krokyleie): accusative singular, proper noun, a place name (elided for *Κροκύλειαν*). *ἐνέμοντο*: 3rd plural imperfect middle of νέμω, "they inhabited/occupied." *Αἰγίλιπα*: accusative singular, proper noun, "Aigilips" (rocky place). *τρηχεῖαν*: accusative singular feminine of τρηχύς, "rugged/rocky," modifying Aigilips. This line continues the catalogue's geographical enumeration, listing those who inhabited Krokyleie and rugged Aigilips.
634:
**οἵ τε Ζάκυνθον ἔχον ἠδʼ οἳ Σάμον ἀμφενέμοντο·**

Key words: **οἵ** (relative pronoun, nominative plural masculine, "those who"), **ἔχον** (imperfect active 3rd plural of ἔχω, "held/possessed"), **ἠδέ** (conjunction, "and"), **ἀμφενέμοντο** (imperfect middle 3rd plural of ἀμφινέμομαι, "dwelt around/occupied"). This line identifies warriors from Zakynthos and those who inhabited the area around Samos (likely Same in Kephallenia).
635:
**ἤπειρον** (acc. sg. fem. of ἤπειρος): "mainland," object of ἔχον. **ἔχον** (3rd pl. imperf. act. indic. of ἔχω): "held, occupied." **ἀντιπέραιʼ** (acc. pl. neut. of ἀντιπέραιος, crasis for ἀντιπέραια): "opposite shores, lands across the water." **ἐνέμοντο** (3rd pl. imperf. mid. indic. of νέμω): "dwelt in, inhabited." 

This line completes the geographical catalog of Odysseus's territories, describing those who held the mainland and inhabited the opposite (coastal) regions.
636:
**τῶν** (gen. pl. of ὅ, ἥ, τό): demonstrative/relative pronoun, "of these" or "of whom," referring to the previously mentioned contingents.

**Ὀδυσσεύς** (nom. sg.): proper name, "Odysseus," subject of the verb.

**ἦρχε** (3rd sg. impf. act. of ἄρχω): "was leading" or "commanded."

**Διί** (dat. sg. of Ζεύς): "to Zeus," dative of comparison.

**μῆτιν** (acc. sg. of μῆτις): "in counsel" or "in wisdom," accusative of respect.

**ἀτάλαντος** (nom. sg. masc. of ἀτάλαντος): "equal to" or "comparable to,"
637:
**Key words:** τῷ (pronoun, dative singular masculine, "with him"), ἕποντο (verb, 3rd plural imperfect middle, "were following"), δυώδεκα (numeral, indeclinable, "twelve"), μιλτοπάρῃοι (adjective, nominative plural feminine, "red-cheeked/vermillion-prowed").

Twelve red-prowed ships followed with Odysseus. The compound μιλτοπάρῃοι literally means "with vermillion at the cheeks/sides," describing ships painted with red ochre on their prows.
638:
**Αἰτωλῶν δʼ ἡγεῖτο Θόας Ἀνδραίμονος υἱός**

Αἰτωλῶν (genitive plural of Αἰτωλοί) "of the Aetolians"; ἡγεῖτο (3rd singular imperfect middle-passive of ἡγέομαι) "was leading, commanded"; Θόας (nominative singular) "Thoas" (personal name); Ἀνδραίμονος (genitive singular of Ἀνδραίμων) "of Andraemon"; υἱός (nominative singular) "son." Thoas, son of Andraemon, led the Aetolian contingent.
639:
**Line:** οἳ Πλευρῶνʼ ἐνέμοντο καὶ Ὤλενον ἠδὲ Πυλήνην

**Gloss:** οἵ (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who" introduces a relative clause identifying the Aetolian warriors. ἐνέμοντο (imperfect mid./pass., 3rd pl. of νέμω) "inhabited, dwelt in" describes their occupation of territory. Πλευρῶνα, Ὤλενον, and Πυλήνην are accusative singular place names (Pleuron, Olenus, Pylene), three Aetolian cities listed in the catalogue.
640:
**Χαλκίδα τʼ ἀγχίαλον Καλυδῶνά τε πετρήεσσαν·**

Χαλκίδα (accusative singular, "Chalcis") and Καλυδῶνα (accusative singular, "Calydon") are cities governed by the Aetolian contingent. ἀγχίαλον (accusative singular adjective, "near the sea") modifies Χαλκίδα; πετρήεσσαν (accusative singular adjective, "rocky") modifies Καλυδῶνα. The τε ... τε construction ("both ... and") coordinates these two prominent Aetolian settlements.
641:
**Gloss for Iliad 2.642:**

**οὐ γάρ** (negative conjunction + explanatory particle): "for not," introducing the reason. **ἔτι** (adverb): "still, any longer." **μεγαλήτορος** (adjective, genitive singular masculine): "great-hearted," modifying Οἰνῆος. **υἱέες** (noun, nominative plural): "sons." **ἦσαν** (verb, 3rd person plural imperfect): "were, existed." 

The line explains that the sons of great-hearted Oeneus were no longer alive, setting up Meleager's death mentioned in the following verse.
642:
**Key words:** οὐδέ (conjunction, "nor, and not"); ἔην (imperfect 3rd sg. εἰμί, "he was"); θάνε (aorist 3rd sg. θνῄσκω, "he died"); ξανθός (nom. sg. masc. adj., "blond, fair-haired"); Μελέαγρος (nom. sg., "Meleager"). 

The line states that Oeneus himself was no longer alive, and that blond Meleager had died, completing the tragic decline of the royal house.
643:
**τῷ** (demonstrative pronoun, dative singular masculine): "to him" (referring to Meleager).
**ἐπὶ ... ἐτέταλτο** (compound pluperfect passive, 3rd singular of ἐπιτέλλω): "had been entrusted/enjoined upon."
**πάντʼ** (neuter plural accusative of πᾶς): "all things."
**ἀνασσέμεν** (present infinitive of ἀνάσσω): "to rule, to be lord over."
**Αἰτωλοῖσι** (dative plural of Αἰτωλός): "the Aetolians."

The line states that all authority to rule the Aetolians had been entrusted to him (Meleager).
644:
**τῷ** (demonstrative pronoun, dative singular masculine): "with him," referring to Thoas as leader of the Aetolians.

**τεσσαράκοντα** (numeral): "forty," modifying νῆες.

**μέλαιναι** (adjective, nominative plural feminine): "black," the conventional epithet for ships, describing their dark-tarred hulls.

**νῆες** (noun, nominative plural): "ships," subject of the verb.

**ἕποντο** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect middle/passive): "were following" or "accompanied," indicating the fleet contingent.

The verse states that forty black ships followed/accompanied Thoas to Troy with the Aetolian forces.
645: **Κρητῶν** (gen. pl. of Κρής): "of the Cretans" - genitive of the people governed by Idomeneus. **Ἰδομενεὺς** (nom. sg.): Idomeneus, the Cretan leader. **δουρὶ κλυτός** (dat. sg. neut. + adj. nom. sg. masc.): "famed for the spear," a formulaic epithet indicating martial prowess. **ἡγεμόνευεν** (3rd sg. impf. act. indic. of ἡγεμονεύω): "was leading/commanded." The line introduces Idomeneus as commander of the Cretan contingent in the Catalogue of Ships.
646:
**Gloss for Iliad 2.646:**

**οἳ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) = "who" – refers to the Cretan contingent. **Κνωσόν** (proper noun, acc. sing.) = "Knossos," the famous Cretan city. **εἶχον** (imperfect act. indic., 3rd pl. of ἔχω) = "held, occupied." **Γόρτυνά** (proper noun, acc. sing.) = "Gortyn," another Cretan city. **τειχιόεσσαν** (adj., acc. sing. fem.) = "well-walled, fortified." The line catalogs the Cretan cities under Idomeneus's command, emphasizing Gortyn's fortifications.
647:
**Λύκτον Μίλητόν τε καὶ ἀργινόεντα Λύκαστον**

Λύκτον: proper noun, accusative singular, Lyctus (Cretan city). Μίλητόν: proper noun, accusative singular, Miletus (Cretan city, not the Ionian one). τε καί: conjunctions, "both...and," connecting the series of cities. ἀργινόεντα: adjective, accusative singular masculine, "bright-white" or "gleaming," modifying Λύκαστον. Λύκαστον: proper noun, accusative singular, Lycastus (Cretan city). The line continues the Cretan catalogue with three more cities under Idomeneus's command, all in accusative as objects of εἶχον.
648: **Φαιστόν** (acc. sg., proper noun) "Phaistos," **Ῥύτιόν** (acc. sg., proper noun) "Rhytion," continuing the catalog of Cretan cities; **πόλεις** (acc. pl., "πόλις") "cities," in apposition to the place names; **εὖ** (adverb) "well"; **ναιετοώσας** (acc. pl. fem. pres. part., "ναιετάω") "dwelling/inhabited." The line lists two well-inhabited Cretan cities, with the participle describing their thriving populations.
649:
**Key words:** ἑκατόμπολιν (accusative singular feminine, compound adjective "hundred-citied" modifying Κρήτην), ἀμφενέμοντο (3rd plural imperfect middle, ἀμφινέμω "to dwell around, inhabit"), Κρήτην (accusative singular, "Crete"), ἄλλοι (nominative plural masculine, "others").

This verse completes the Cretan catalogue, describing how "others who dwelt around hundred-citied Crete" served under Idomeneus's command; the compound ἑκατόμπολιν emphasizes Crete's legendary wealth of cities.
650:
**Key words:** τῶν (demonstrative pronoun, genitive plural) "of these/them"; Ἰδομενεύς (proper noun, nominative singular) "Idomeneus"; δουρί (noun, dative singular) "in/with the spear," instrumental dative; κλυτός (adjective, nominative singular masculine) "famous, renowned"; ἡγεμόνευε (verb, third singular imperfect active) "was leading, commanded." 

Of these Cretans, Idomeneus, famous with the spear, was the commander.
